And when his whole structure is raised up, consummated, and perfected, then he becomes a house and a temple for a dwelling-place of Christ, as Jeremiah the Prophet said:—The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord are ye, if ye amend your ways and your works. And again He said through the Prophet:—I will dwell in them and walk in them. And also the Blessed Apostle thus said:—Ye are the temple of God and the spirit of Christ dwelleth in you. And also our Lord again thus said to His disciples:—Ye are in Me and I am in you.

Do not trust in lying words, saying: The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord it is! For if you direct well — or direct — your ways and your pursuits, if you execute judgment between a man and his neighbor, if you do not practice false accusation against the stranger and the orphan and the widow — or do not oppress them — and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not walk after strange gods to your own harm, I will dwell with you — or I will make you dwell — in this place, in the land which I gave to your fathers from age to age. This, which the Seventy added at the beginning of this chapter: in words of falsehood, which will not profit you at all, is not found in the Hebrew. He commands both the people of the Jews then and us today, who seem to be established in the Church, not to have confidence in the splendor of buildings and in gilded ceilings and in walls clad with veneers of marble, and say: the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord it is. […]

Then what value can our claim to a religious title have for us, what use is it to say we are catholic, to boast that we possess the true faith, to despise the Goths and Vandals, reviling them as heretics, when we are living in a truly heretical depravity? The words of the Divine Scripture addressed to the Jews who trusted in the law are most fittingly applied to us: "How do you say, 'We are wise and the law of the Lord is with us?' . . . Trust ye not in lying words, saying, 'The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, are these.' For if ye thoroughly amend your ways and your doings; if ye oppress not the stranger and the fatherless and the widow and shed not innocent blood in this place, then will I cause you to dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers for ever and ever.'' By this surely it is shown that if we do not amend our ways, it is useless for us to vaunt our claims to Catholicism.
7:4.s: On the Government of God, Book 7, Chapter 11

7:5.t: Then he adds: 'if you make your ways straight, and your thought does not go off after error, and you follow righteousness and do not commit evil, and do not shed innocent blood by scandalizing every simple person, and do not walk after strange gods by worshipping perverse doctrines which you have feigned out of your own heart to your own harm, then either I will dwell with you in this place, which you call the temple of God, and in the land which I gave to your fathers, namely the apostles and apostolic men, or at any rate with a firm standing I will make you dwell from the beginning to the end.' This can also suit those virgins who boast of their chastity and display purity with a shameless face, while their conscience holds something else, and who do not know that definition of virginity given by the Apostle, that she be holy in body and in spirit. For what does purity of body profit when the mind has been debauched, if she does not have the other virtues which the prophetic word has described?

7:8.t: Behold, you trust in words of falsehood — or lying words —, which will not profit you: to steal, to kill, to commit adultery, to swear falsely, to pour libations to the Baals, and to go after strange gods whom you do not know. And you came and stood before me in this house, in which my name has been called upon, and you said: We are delivered — or we have ceased — because we have done all these abominations. The sins that follow show that they have confidence in the temple in vain. For what does it profit to cross boldly the threshold of the house of God, to stand with neck held high, and to have not only the heart but also the hands polluted with theft, murder, adultery, perjury, sacrilege, and the worship of those gods whom you do not know? No one doubts that this happens spiritually in the Church, when people, considering the prosperity of the present time, do not take account of their sins and think that they are hidden from God, because punishment does not follow at once; […]

7:11.t: Wherefore, brethren, if we do the will of God our Father, we shall be of the first Church, that is, spiritual, that hath been created before the sun and moon; but if we do not the will of the Lord, we shall be of the scripture that saith, "My house was made a den of robbers." So then let us choose to be of the Church of life, that we may be saved.
7:11.s: Second Epistle to the Corinthians (2 Clement), 14

7:11.t: Has this house — or my house —, in which my name has been called upon, become a den of robbers in your eyes? I, I am, I have seen, says the Lord. From this passage, I think, was taken what is in the Gospel: It is written: My Father's house shall be called a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers, or, as is written in another Gospel, a house of trade. The Church of God is turned into a den of robbers when theft, murder, adultery, perjury, sacrilege, the invention of heresy and every crime are at home in it, when princes burn with the torches of avarice and a cheap, or at any rate not cheap, little cloak possesses what were once the riches of kings. Hence he adds: 'I, I am, I have seen, says the Lord; my eyes have beheld what you think hidden; the darkness of your treasuries does not escape my knowledge'. He who, though he was rich, became poor for our sake, now blushes at our riches and says: Woe to you rich, who have your consolation!

7:12.t: Go to my place in Shiloh, where my name dwelt from the beginning, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel! From the past he teaches the present, and to those who say: the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord and who rejoice in the gleam of a costly house he recalls the history of Shiloh, where the tabernacle of God first was, of which it is written in the psalm: and he rejected the tabernacle of Shiloh, so that, just as that place collapsed into ruins and ashes, so the temple too may fall, since it has been the dwelling of like sins. Therefore, just as Shiloh is an example for the temple, so is the temple for us, when the time of that testimony comes: Do you think the Son of Man, when he comes, will find faith on the earth?

7:13.t: And now, because you have done all these works, says the Lord, and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, and you did not hear, and I called you and you did not answer, I will do to this house, in which my name has been called upon and in which you have confidence, and to the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I did to Shiloh, and I will cast you out from my face, as I cast out all your brothers, the whole seed of Ephraim. This which we have set down: rising early and speaking, is not found in the Seventy. Now God rises early, not because there is any time for him without daybreak, but because after the rest of the night, when the strength of the body has been restored, the soul of men is more vigorous and, in no way occupied with pleasures and the desire for food, is able to hear and to do what is said. Hence we also read this in the psalm: In the morning you will hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before you and will see; […]

7:14.t: Since, therefore, God called them, rising by night, so that he might free them too from darkness, he threatens them that he will do to the temple in Jerusalem things like those he did to the place Shiloh, where the tabernacle first was, so that like sins may be struck by an equal sentence. And just as the Lord cast out the seed of Ephraim, that is, the ten tribes, which were called Israel and had princes on account of Jeroboam son of Nebat, of the tribe of Ephraim, which was likewise called the tribe of Joseph, so he testifies that he will also cast away Jerusalem and the tribe of Judah with Benjamin. He cast away Shiloh, therefore, and he will cast away the temple too; he cast away the ten tribes, and he will cast away the two as well. Whatever is said to that people, let us understand it of ourselves too, if we do like things.

7:16.t: Rightly, then, is it said, "Who shall entreat for him?" It implies that it must be such a one as Moses to offer himself for those who sin. Or such as Jeremiah, who, though the Lord said to him, "Pray not for this people," yet prayed and obtained their forgiveness. For at the intercession of the prophet and the entreaty of so great a seer, the Lord was moved. And Jerusalem, which had meanwhile repented for its sins, had said, "O Almighty Lord God of Israel, the soul in anguish and the troubled spirit cries to you. Hear, O Lord, and have mercy."

And with regard to the deluge again He did the self-same thing, by His acts excusing Himself to Noah. And also to Ezekiel in like manner, when He caused him dwelling in Babylon to see men's evil deeds in Jerusalem. And yet again to Jeremiah, when He said, "Pray not," excusing Himself He added, "Seest thou not what they do?" And everywhere He doeth the selfsame thing, as here also. For what saith He? "The men of Nineveh shall rise up, and shall condemn this generation, because they repented at the preaching of Jonas, and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here."
7:16.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 43:3

7:16.t: You, therefore, do not pray for this people, nor take up praise and prayer for them — or nor ask that they obtain mercy, — and do not withstand me, for I will not hear you. So that the prophet may not seem, in asking, to fail to obtain what he requests, God commands him not to intercede for a sinful people that does no repentance at all. But when he says: and do not resist me, he shows this, that the prayers of the saints can resist the wrath of God. Hence the Lord also speaks to Moses: Let me go, that I may strike this people, and I will make you into a great nation; and in the Psalms it is written: And Phinehas stood and appeased, and the shaking ceased, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness. Aaron too, seizing a censer, stood in the midst between the fire and the people about to burn, and the wrath of God ceased. And lest we think God cruel, since he does not even allow himself to be entreated, he gives the reasons why he does not hear, saying:

7:17.t: You will find at least in the book of Jeremiah the words of God censuring by the mouth of the prophet the Jewish people for doing obeisance to such objects and for sacrificing to the queen of heaven and to all the host of heaven. The writings of the Christians, moreover, show, in censuring the sins committed among the Jews, that when God abandoned that people on account of certain sins, these sins of idol worship also were committed by them.

Do you not see what these are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? The sons gather wood and the fathers kindle the fire and the women sprinkle fat, to make cakes — or chauonas — for the queen — or the host — of heaven, and to pour libations to strange gods and to provoke me to anger. Is it me they provoke to anger? says the Lord, is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own face? 'Do you wish,' he says, 'to hear, prophet, why I said to you: do not pray for this people? They do these things that follow: both within and without and in the streets and in the outlets of Jerusalem the sons carry together wood and the fathers kindle the fire and the women sprinkle fat with flour to make chauonim' — which we have rendered 'cakes' or 'preparations', so that it shows every kind of sacrifice to the queen of heaven, whom we should take to be the moon, or at any rate to the host of heaven, so that we understand all the stars — 'and after this they pour libations to strange gods, not that these […]

7:18.t: For "God" is "jealous" and does not wish the soul which he has betrothed to himself in faith to remain in the defilement of sin, but wishes her quickly to be purged, wishes her swiftly to cast off all her uncleannesses, if perhaps anything has stolen upon her. But if she remain in sins and say: we will not hear the voice of the Lord, but doing we will do our own wills and will burn offerings "to the queen of heaven", as is reproached through the prophet: then she too is reserved for that sentence of wisdom which says: "since indeed I called and you would not hear, but mocked my words; therefore I too will laugh at your destruction", or for that which is set before them in the Gospel, the Lord saying: "depart from me into eternal fire, which God has prepared for the devil and his angels".

For this is why He at all threatens punishment; that by fear He may destroy contempt; and when the threat alone is sufficient to cause fear in us, He doth not suffer us to undergo the actual trial. See, for instance, what He saith unto Jeremiah, "Seest thou not what they do? Their fathers light a fire, their children gather sticks together, their women knead dough." It is to be feared lest the same kind of thing be said also concerning us. "Seest thou not what they do? No one seeketh the things of Christ, but all their own. Their children run into uncleanness, their fathers into covetousness and rapine, their wives so far from keeping back their husbands from the pomps and vanities of life, do rather sharpen their appetites for them."
Chabonim: hand, or a heap of thorns. But better: preparations, although most of the Hebrews think that offering-cakes or little pastries are meant.

7:20.t: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, my fury and my indignation is kindled — or has dripped — upon this place, upon men and upon beasts and upon the trees of the region and upon the fruits of the earth, and it will be set alight and will not be quenched. He who had said above: Is it me they provoke to anger?, how does he now say: Behold, my fury and my indignation has dripped upon this place? And the sense is: 'I indeed am not angered by nature, but they act in such a way as to provoke me to anger, so that I seem to change my nature. Let them, therefore, feel me angry, which, so far as in them lies, they are trying to bring about.' And beautifully he does not say: 'has been poured out' my fury upon this place, but: has dripped, so as to signify a moderate punishment. But if in a drop of fury there is such harshness, what will happen if the whole downpour is poured out? But 'kindling' too can be understood thus: that what he long did not wish to do, he is compelled to do by the multitude of sins. […]

7:21.t: HOW HAS THE LORD IN LEVITICUS COMMANDED THAT SACRIFICES AND LIBATIONS BE OFFERED, WHICH ELSEWHERE HE REJECTS? FOR IT IS CLEAR IN LEVITICUS THAT THE LORD COMMANDED THE FATHERS TO OFFER LIBATIONS OR SACRIFICES OR BURNT OFFERINGS: YET HE SAYS THEREFORE THROUGH THE PROPHET JEREMIAH: THEREFORE SAYS THE LORD, GATHER YOUR BURNT OFFERINGS WITH YOUR SACRIFICES, AND EAT FLESH; FOR I DID NOT SPEAK TO YOUR FATHERS, NOR DID I COMMAND THEM, IN THE DAY THAT I BROUGHT THEM OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT (Jer. 7:21–22) ABOUT BURNT OFFERINGS AND SACRIFICES. — If you look closely, there is really no question to be raised on this matter; nor should you think the Lord lied or changed, as if he commanded and later denied. For of this kind of sacrifices and drink offerings or burnt offerings, nothing is found that he commanded, regarding those of which he now testifies that he spoke. Notice that there are two kinds of sacrifices: one which was commanded to be offered for each specific kind, and another which was called voluntary. […]
7:21.s: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 103: WHY GOD COMMANDS SACRIFICES YET ELSEWHERE REJECTS THEM

7:21.t: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Add your burnt offerings to your victims and eat flesh, for I did not speak with your fathers, and I did not command them on the day that I led them out of the land of Egypt, concerning the matter of burnt offerings and victims, but this word I commanded them, saying: Hear my voice, and I will be your God and you will be my people, and walk in every way that I have commanded you, that it may be well with you. Having rejected their temple, he consequently rejects their sacrifices too, and indirectly reproves them because they sacrifice victims not out of reverence for him but out of desire for feasting. […]

7:22.t: He has therefore abolished these things, that the new law of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is without the yoke of necessity, might have a human oblation. And again He says to them, "Did I command your fathers, when they went out from the land of Egypt, to offer unto Me burnt-offerings and sacrifices? But this rather I commanded them, Let no one of you cherish any evil in his heart against his neighbour, and love not an oath of falsehood." We ought therefore, being possessed of understanding, to perceive the gracious intention of our Father; for He speaks to us, desirous that we, not going astray like them, should ask how we may approach Him. To us, then, He declares, "A sacrifice [pleasing] to God is a broken spirit; a smell of sweet savour to the Lord is a heart that glorifieth Him that made it." We ought therefore, brethren, carefully to inquire concerning our salvation, lest the wicked one, having made his entrance by deceit, should hurl us forth from our [true] life.
7:22.s: The Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter II

7:22.t: And what does this mean my brethren? For it is right for us to investigate the saying of the prophet, and especially on account of heretics who have turned their mind against the law. By Moses then, God gave commandment respecting sacrifices, and all the book called Leviticus is entirely taken up with the arrangement of these matters, so that He might accept the offerer. So through the Prophets, He blames him who despised these things, as disobedient to the commandment saying, ‘I have not required these at your hands. Neither did I speak to your fathers respecting sacrifices, nor command them concerning whole burnt-offerings.’ Now it is the opinion of some, that the Scriptures do not agree together, or that God, Who gave the commandment, is false. But there is no disagreement whatever, far from it, neither can the Father, Who is truth, lie; ‘for it is impossible that God should lie,’ as Paul affirms. […]

7:23.t: In a manner most germane to this parable, He said by Jeremiah: "Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people; and ye shall walk in all my ways, which I have commanded you." This is the invitation of God. "But," says He, "they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear." This is the refusal of the people. "They departed, and walked every one in the imagination of their evil heart." "I have bought a field-and I have bought some oxen-and I have married a wife." And still He urges them: "I have sent unto you all my servants the prophets, rising early even before day-light." The Holy Spirit is here meant, the admonisher of the guests. "Yet my people hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear, but hardened their neck."
7:23.s: The Five Books Against Marcion, Book 4

7:24.t: And they did not hear nor incline their ear, but they went off in the wills — or desires — and the depravity of their evil heart, and they became backward and not forward, from the day on which their fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day. 'When I said: Hear my voice and I will be your God and the rest, they did not hear nor incline their ear, but they did the desires of their own heart, and against the judgment of the Apostle, who forgot what lay behind and stretched himself toward what lay before, they did the contrary, so as to desire the past and despise the future.' And when he says: from the day on which their fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day, he says that they spent all the time in between in offense against the Lord. Hence the grace of the Gospel was also necessary, which saved them not by their own merit but by the mercy of the Lord.

7:25.t: And I sent to you my servants, the prophets, by day, rising at daybreak and sending; and they did not hear me nor incline their ear, but they hardened their neck and wrought worse than their fathers. Just, therefore, is the wrath of the Lord, which has been kindled and has dripped upon a contemptuous and stiff-necked people that refuses to hear the words of God. But how God sends the prophets either by night or at daybreak and by day, we have said above.

7:27.t: And you will speak to them all these words, and they will not hear you; and you will call them, and they will not answer you. And you will say to them: This is the nation that has not heard the voice of the Lord its God nor received discipline; faith has perished and has been taken away from their mouth. 'Do not doubt,' he says, 'that they have hardened their neck and wrought worse than their fathers; behold, I give room for repentance, and I do not speak in order that these things may happen, but because they are going to happen, therefore I foretell them. At least now speak to them with my words, and yet they will not hear you; and you will call them, and they will not answer you; for they will be of such pride that, when you call them to hear, no one will deign to answer. And you will say to them: This is the nation that has not heard the voice of the Lord its God nor received discipline'. Beautifully, as I have already said before, he calls them not at all his people, but a nation. […]

7:29.t: But last of all He sent to those unbelievers His own Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, whom the wicked husbandmen cast out of the vineyard when they had slain Him. Wherefore the Lord God did even give it up (no longer hedged around, but thrown open throughout all the world) to other husbandmen, who render the fruits in their seasons—the beautiful elect tower being also raised everywhere. For the illustrious Church is [now] everywhere, and everywhere is the winepress digged: because those who do receive the Spirit are everywhere. For inasmuch as the former have rejected the Son of God, and cast Him out of the vineyard when they slew Him, God has justly rejected them, and given to the Gentiles outside the vineyard the fruits of its cultivation. This is in accordance with what Jeremiah says, "The Lord hath rejected and cast off the nation which does these things; for the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, saith the Lord."

Shear your hair and cast it away, and take up in the open — or upon the lips — a lament, for the Lord has cast off and forsaken the generation of his fury. We read that Job too, on hearing of the death of his sons and daughters, sheared his hair, and among the ancients this was the custom of all who mourned, to shear the locks; but now, on the contrary, to let the hair grow long is the sign of mourning. And all the prophet's lament and lamentation is taken up for this reason, for the Lord has cast off and forsaken the generation of his fury; no doubt he signifies the people of the Jews. And this is properly to be referred to the times of Christ, when faith perished and was taken away from the mouth of the people blaspheming the Lord.

7:30.t: For the sons of Judah have done evil in my sight, says the Lord; they have set their stumbling blocks in the house in which my name has been called upon, to pollute it, and they have built the high places — or the altar — of Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters with fire, which I did not command nor think of in my heart. That the sons of Judah set up a statue of Baal in the temple of God we learn at the beginning of Ezekiel. Now 'high places', which in Hebrew are called 'bamath', or 'altar' of Topheth, which is in the valley of the sons of Hinnom, signifies that place which is watered by the springs of Siloam, and is pleasant and wooded, and to this day offers the delights of gardens. And this error of paganism took hold of all the provinces, so that they sacrificed victims at the heads of springs and in the loveliest groves, and the observance of every depraved superstition was kept. […]

7:32.t: Ennom [Hinnom]: behold these, or they are.
Thof [Topheth]: Gehenna, or covering of the mouth.

Therefore, behold, the days will come, says the Lord, and it will no longer be called Topheth and the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of killing, and they will bury in Topheth because there is no room. And the carcasses of this people will be food for the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and there will be none to drive them away. He signifies the time of the siege, which they endured from the ninth year of King Zedekiah to the eleventh year, and that the valley itself will by no means be called 'gehennom', that is, 'valley of hennom', or 'of the sons of Hinnom', but, on account of the killing of very many, 'valley of slaughter'. And so great will the slaughter be that in the place formerly of worship there will be innumerable tombs, and those whom they cannot bury will be torn by birds and devoured by beasts, and there will be no one to drive them away, since he fears the like and is overcome by the duties of burying. […]

7:34.t: And I will make to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, and the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land will be in desolation. When the place of idolatry has been turned into tombs, so that where they had offended God, there their corpses lie unburied, all gladness will be taken away from the city of Jerusalem that once was and from the other cities that were under its dominion, and all things will be filled with sorrow and groaning and desolation.

8:1.t: At that time, says the Lord, they shall cast out the bones of the king of Judah and the bones of his princes and the bones of the priests and the bones of the prophets and the bones of those who dwelt in Jerusalem, from their graves. And they shall spread them out to the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which they have loved and which they have served and after which they have walked and which they have sought and worshiped. They shall not be gathered and shall not be buried; they shall be for a dunghill upon the face of the earth. And all who remain of this most wicked family shall choose death rather than life, in all the places that are left, to which I have cast them out, says the Lord of hosts. All the things that the prophetic word describes we see to have happened in our own time, not to Jerusalem alone, which suffered these things from the Chaldeans and the Romans, but to the whole world, so that tears have dried up and everything has been filled with the bones of the dead. […]

8:4.t: And pray ye without ceasing in behalf of other men; for there is hope of the repentance, that they may attain to God. For "cannot he that falls arise again, and he that goes astray return?" Permit them, then, to be instructed by you. Be ye therefore the ministers of God, and the mouth of Christ. For thus saith the Lord, "If ye take forth the precious from the vile, ye shall be as my mouth." Be ye humble in response to their wrath; oppose to their blasphemies your earnest prayers; while they go astray, stand ye stedfast in the faith. Conquer ye their harsh temper by gentleness, their passion by meekness. For "blessed are the meek"; and Moses was meek above all men; and David was exceeding meek.
8:4.s: Epistle of Ignatius to the Ephesians

8:4.t: If you have any hope of salvation; if you have the least thought of God, or any desire for good things to come; if you have any fear of the chastisements reserved for the impenitent, awake without delay, lift up your eyes to heaven, come to your senses, cease from your wickedness, shake off the stupor that enwraps you, make a stand against the foe who has struck you down. Make an effort to rise from the ground. Remember the good Shepherd who will follow and rescue you. Though it be but two legs or a lobe of an ear, spring back from the beast that has wounded you. Remember the mercies of God and how He cures with oil and wine. Do not despair of salvation. Recall your recollection of how it is written in the Scriptures that he who is falling rises and he who turns away returns; the wounded is healed, the prey of beasts escapes; he who owns his sin is not rejected. The Lord willeth not the death of a sinner but rather that he should turn and live.

Doth not David say, Every night I will wash my bed, I will water my couch with my tears; and again, I acknowledge my sin, and mine unrighteousness have I not hid; and yet more, I said, I will confess my sins unto the Lord, and so Thou forgavest the wickedness of my heart. Did not the Prophet answer him when, after the guilt of murder and adultery, penitent for Bathsheba, The Lord also hath put away from thee thy sin? Did not confession deliver the king of Babylon, when condemned after so many sins of idolatry? And what is it that the Lord saith, Shall he who has fallen not arise, and he who has turned not return?

Behold! I promise, I engage, if ye return to your Father with true satisfaction, erring no more, adding nothing to former sins, saying also some humble and mournful words, as, Father, we have sinned before Thee, and are no more worthy to be called Thy sons; straightway shall leave you both that filthy herd, and the unseemly food of husks. Straightway on your return shall the robe be put upon you, and the ring adorn you, and your Father's embrace again receive you. Lo! He saith Himself, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that he turn from his way and live. And again He saith, Shall they fall, and not arise? Shall he turn away, and not return? And the Apostle saith, God is able to make him stand.

Now then is it not strange that, whilst others do not even now despair of thy salvation, but are continually praying that they may have their member restored to them, thou thyself, having once fallen, art unwilling to get up again, and remainest prostrate, all but crying aloud to the enemy: "Slay me, smite me, spare not?" "Does he who falls not rise up again?" speaks the divine oracle. But thou art striving against this and contradicting it; for if one who has fallen despairs it is as much as to say that he who falls does not rise up again. I entreat thee do not so great a wrong to thyself; do not pour upon us such a flood of sorrow. […]

And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Shall he who falls not rise again? And he who has turned away, shall he not return — or shall he not turn away — ? After such great evils he calls to repentance those who were able to remain, or before they come. He has threatened these things; he exhorts them to conversion and gives room for repentance. But what is written according to the Hebrew: and he who has turned away, shall he not turn away, signifies this: that he who has turned away from God, if he is willing to be converted to better things, can also turn the fury of God to better things, and withstand what is coming, and escape the blows by prayers.

8:5.t: They have all abandoned him. There is no one who speaks well and does penance for his sins. They follow their own wills like a horse ready for battle. They bend their tongue as a bow. They invent everything, and there is no truth in them.

Why then has this people in Jerusalem turned away with a contentious turning away? They have laid hold of falsehood and they would not return? 'The more I,' he says, 'called them to repentance, the more they withdrew from me, not so much from eagerness to sin as from eagerness to overcome me. For they have laid hold firmly of falsehood, whether idols or whatever perverse things are contrary to truth and righteousness, and they would not return' — he did not say 'they could not' —, 'but with all eagerness they have pursued wicked things'.

8:6.t: Wherefore it were meet exceedingly to admire the consideration of our Lawgiver, in that, when He might bring forward His illustration from among men, and when He might have spoken of Moses and Elias and John, and others like them, who took no thought; that He might touch them more to the quick, He made mention of the irrational beings. For had He spoken of those righteous men, these would have been able to say, "We are not yet become like them." But now by passing them over in silence, and bringing forward the fowls of the air, He hath cut off from them every excuse, imitating in this place also the old law. Yea, for the old covenant likewise sends to the bee, and to the ant, and to the turtle, and to the swallow. And neither is this a small sign of honor, when the same sort of things, which those animals possess by nature, those we are able to accomplish by an act of our choice.
8:6.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 21:4

8:6.t: I attended and listened; no one speaks what is good, there is none who does repentance over his sin, saying: What have I done? All have turned to their course, like a horse going with a rush to battle. Called back to repentance, they scorn to listen; nor is it enough for them to have offended against the Lord and to have spoken blasphemy, but all, like horses rushing in hot course to battle, do not reflect on their sin nor say: what have I done? By which we understand that these things are said either of the whole human race, because it is prone to vices, or of the time of the Savior, when all have turned aside, together they have become useless; there was none who did good, there was not even one. Hence he himself also cries out mystically: save me, O Lord, for the holy one has failed! But if these things are so, where are those who say that it lies within our will to be free of all sin? No one, he says, speaks what is good, because we shall render account even for an idle word on the day of judgment.

8:7.t:
The Lord gave utterance to these words in the book of Jeremias: ‘The turtle and the swallow and the sparrows of the field observed the time of their coming, but my people have not known the judgments of the Lord.’ Swallows know the time of their coming and of their return. These dutiful birds know how to announce the signs of spring by the testimony of their arrival.

Ants also keep watch for the coming of sunny weather. When they notice that their store of food remains soggy because of rain storms, a careful exploration is made of atmospheric conditions to determine when a series of warm days should arrive. Then they release the food supply, which is carried out of their hiding places to be dried by prolonged exposure to the sun. For that reason you will never experience stormy weather during that whole period of time, except when it should, in the interval, happen that the ants have changed their minds and decided to restore their supply of food to their granaries. […]

The kite in the heaven has known its time; the turtledove and the swallow and the stork have kept the time of their coming; but my people has not known the judgment of the Lord. For 'kite', which Symmachus translated, the Seventy and Theodotion put the Hebrew word itself, 'asida', Aquila 'herodiona' [heron]. And again for 'swallow' Symmachus translated 'cicada', which in Hebrew is called 'sis'. And for what we have put as 'stork', both Aquila and Symmachus translated 'agur', just as it is written in the Hebrew, for which the Seventy translated 'sparrows of the field'. And it is one and the same sense which is also set down at the beginning of Isaiah: the ox has known its owner and the ass the manger of its master, but Israel has not known me and my people has not understood; namely, that even small birds know their seasons and know when, hastening to warm places, they ought to escape the harshness of winter, and again at the beginning of spring come back to their accustomed regions. […]

8:8.t: How do you say: We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us? Truly the lying pen of the scribes has wrought falsehood. He speaks to the scribes and Pharisees, who boast of their knowledge of the law and, writing, write iniquity. And as for what he says:

Nor is it in my opinion unreasonable to add also the following. The Scribes and Pharisees, who held high rank among the Jews, as having the reputation of legal learning, were regarded as wise men. But they were convicted by the very result of not being so in reality. For even the prophet Jeremiah thus somewhere addressed them: "How say ye, that we are wise, and the word of the Lord is with us? The lying cord of the scribe is for emptiness. The wise men are ashamed; they fear and are taken: what wisdom is in. them, because they have rejected the word of the Lord?" Because then they rejected the word of the Saviour, that is, the saving message of the Gospel, or in other language, the Word of God the Father, Who for our sakes became man, they have themselves been rejected.
8:8.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

8:8.t: THE blessed prophet Jeremiah loudly condemned the ignorance, at once, and pride of the Jews, rebuking them in these words; "How say you that we are wise, and the word of the Lord is with us? In vain is the lying cord of the scribes. The wise men are ashamed: they trembled, and were taken: what wisdom have they, in that they have rejected the Word of the Lord!" For being neither wise, nor acquainted with the sacred Scriptures, though the scribes and Pharisees falsely assumed to themselves the reputation of being learned in the law, they rejected the Word of God. For when the Only Begotten had become man, they did not receive Him, nor yield their neck obediently to the summons which He addressed to them by the Gospel. Because therefore by their wicked conduct they rejected the Word of God, they were themselves rejected, being condemned by God's just decree. For He said, by the voice of Jeremiah, "Call them rejected silver: because the Lord has rejected them." […]
8:8.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

8:9.t: The wise are confounded, terrified and taken, it is not that those who do these things are wise, but he calls them wise so that they may be condemned by their own judgment and, on the contrary, their wisdom may be proved to be folly, as Paul says: you who teach another, do you not teach yourself? And because they have cast away the word of the Lord, therefore there is no wisdom in them. In vain, then, do they boast of knowledge of the law who destroy their teaching by their works.

Finally, whoever wishes fuller proof that mere words are nothing without actions should consider how countless peoples, by failing in good works, have lost the names given them. The twelve tribes of the Hebrews, when they were of old chosen by God, received two holy names, for they were called the people of God, and Israel. We read: "Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee." Once the Jews bore both these titles, now they have neither. They who long since left off the worship of God cannot be called God's people, nor can they who denied his Son be given a name that means "Seeing God." So it is written: "But Israel does not know, my people doth not consider."

For this reason on another occasion our God spoke of the people of the Hebrews to the prophet, saying: "Call his name, Not Beloved." And speaking to the Jews themselves: "You are not my people and I am not your God." […]
8:9.s: On the Government of God, Book 4, Chapter 1

8:10.t: Therefore I will give their women — or wives — to strangers, their fields to heirs, because from the least to the greatest all are devoted to avarice, from the prophet to the priest all practice falsehood — or iniquity —. And they healed the breaking of the daughter of my people to ignominy, saying: Peace, peace, when there was not peace. They received the wages of their works, so that those who cast away the word of the Lord were themselves cast away by him. 'Their wives,' he says, 'and their possessions I will hand over to the enemy. And lest my sentence be thought cruel, let the hearer recognize the causes: from the least to the greatest all are devoted to avarice — for avarice is the root of all evils —, from the prophet to the priest. Those who ought to restrain others when they sin are the first to be given over to crimes, and all either do iniquitous things, while they plunder the goods of others, or at any rate practice falsehood, so that there is no truth in their mouth.

8:11.t: The arranged time comes to our people; there is peace in the world; and, at the same time, ruin is weighing us down from the enticement of the world, (the destruction) of the reckless people whom you have rent into schism. Either obey the law of the city, or depart from it. You behold the mote sticking in our eyes, and will not see the beam in your own. A treacherous peace is coming to you; persecution is rife; the wounds do not appear; and thus, without slaughter, you are destroyed. War is waged in secret, because, in the midst of peace itself, scarcely one of you has behaved himself with caution. O badly fortified, and foretold for slaughter, you praise a treacherous peace, a peace that is mischievous to you. Having become the soldiers of another than Christ, you have perished.

Do not believe the false prophets who say, "Peace, peace, and there is no peace"; who are always repeating, "The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord." "Your prophets have seen for you false and foolish things; they have not laid bare your iniquity that they might call you to repentance—those who devour God's people like bread have not called on God." Jeremiah announced the captivity and was [punished] by the people. Hananiah, the son of Azzur, broke the bars of wood for the present but was preparing bars of iron for the future. False prophets always promise pleasant things, and please for a fee. Truth is bitter, however, and those who preach it are filled with bitterness. For with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth the Lord's Passover is kept, and it is eaten with bitter herbs.

And after these things, like good physicians, they desired to heal the wounds of others with words, they who were themselves pierced through with the wounds of every shameful deed'. This we see daily in our own people too, as the Apostle says: you who preach that one must not steal, do you steal? and the rest. When these see sinners and rich men, they desire to heal the breaking of the daughter of the people of God, that is, of the Church, to the ignominy either of those who are deceived or of those who deceive others, so that they say to men covered with every crime: peace, peace, when there is no peace, while the war of their sins hangs over them.

8:12.t: Were they confounded, because they committed abomination? Nay rather, they were not confounded with confusion, and they did not know how to blush. This is to be read Erōtēmatikōs [as a question], so that the sense is: 'Did they blush in their crimes, did they understand the abominations which they wrought?' 'By no means; but they burst out into such madness that they neither desired to amend their vices through confusion nor to confess their crimes in hope of pardon'.

Therefore they shall fall among those who collapse; in the time of their visitation they shall collapse, says the Lord. These are the rewards of those who did not know how to blush: that those whose dignity was loftier than the peoples should be mingled in the ruins of the people. For from the least to the greatest all are devoted to avarice, and from the prophet to the priest all practice falsehood; and the time of visitation is the approaching captivity.

8:13.t: Gathering I will gather them, says the Lord; there is no grape on the vines and there are no figs on the fig tree; the leaf has fallen, and I have given them things that have passed by. What the time of visitation is, in which the transgressors shall collapse, he teaches more plainly, saying: 'Gathering I will gather them' — no doubt in Jerusalem —, 'so that they may be besieged by the Chaldeans for a long time and endure the evils of famine. When,' he says, 'the seasons pass, and autumn follows summer, and in winter the leaves of the trees fall, you will see everything from afar and from them you will take no food. There is no indeed grape on the vines for you, who do not take the fruit of the vines, and there are no figs on the fig tree for the besieged people, who sees the fruits of its own trees plundered by the enemy. The leaves,' he says, 'will fall when summer and autumn are past. […]

8:14.t: Why do we sit still? Come together, and let us enter the fortified city — or the fortified cities — and let us be silent there — or let us be cast out there —, for our Lord has cast us off — or has made us silent — and has given us water of gall to drink; for we have sinned against the Lord. We waited for peace, and there was no good, for a time of healing, and behold, dread. The voice of the people is brought in, answering and confessing its vices and exhorting one another to enter the walled cities, or the one city Jerusalem; for the rest had already been taken. 'And let us be silent', he says, 'there, for our Lord has made us silent — for we have no confidence to pray —, or let us be cast away there or let us be cast out like dung. He himself has made us drink waters of gall, because we turned God, who is sweet, into bitterness. […]

8:16.t: From Dan was heard the snorting of his horses, at the sound of the neighings of his fighters — or of his cavalry — the whole land was shaken; and they came and devoured — or and they will come and will devour — the land and its fullness, the city and its inhabitants. So the people did not say, as the Seventy translated above: let us enter the fortified cities, but: the fortified city, so as to signify Jerusalem. And indeed he now also adds: the city and its inhabitants. Nebuchadnezzar is described coming with his army from Dan, through Phoenicia, at which place the river Jordan rises; and what the Seventy give as things to come, the Hebrew, in accordance with the truth of the event, records as already done.

8:17.t: For behold, I will send among you serpents, basilisks — or most wicked or, as the Seventy translated, deadly —, for which there is no charm; and they shall bite you, says the Lord, incurably, with the pain of your failing heart. Who those are who come from Dan, and whose snorting was heard, and who reduced the whole land to a wilderness, the same prophetic word shows under another figure, calling them 'serpents', 'most wicked' or 'deadly', and, as Aquila translated, 'basilisks', which are called in Hebrew 'sapphonim'; for which I do not understand what his second edition meant by saying 'watchmen', unless perhaps because of the similarity of the word. For which there is no, he says, charm. For in vain do they pour out prayers to God against the ancient serpent, the twisting snake, who have scorned the commandments of God. Let us use this passage against those who, scorning the sayings of the Savior, are handed over to the adverse powers.

However you should know that the evil of envy is harder to be cured than other faults, for I should almost say that a man whom it has once tainted with the mischief of its poison is without a remedy. For it is the plague of which it is figuratively said by the prophet: "Behold I will send among you serpents, basilisks, against which there is no charm: and they shall bite you." Rightly then are the stings of envy compared by the prophet to the deadly poison of basilisks, as by it the first author of all poisons and their chief perished and died. For he slew himself before him of whom he was envious, and destroyed himself before that he poured forth the poison of death against man: for "by the envy of the devil death entered into the world: they therefore who are on his side follow him." […]

8:18.t: My pain is above pain, within me my heart is mourning. For this, as we said above, the Seventy joined what is said to the preceding sentence, so as to put: and they shall bite you, says the Lord, incurably, with the pain of your failing heart. But in the Hebrew there is not so much 'pain', which in Greek is called odynē, as meidiama, which we can translate as the 'grimace' of a mouth contracted by pain and having the likeness of a smile. And these things are to be read Emphatikōs [emphatically] as from the person of God, lamenting the overthrow of Jerusalem and not bearing her miseries.

8:19.t: Behold the voice of the crying of the daughter of my people from a land far off! He describes the weeping and wailing of the city of Jerusalem when the enemy had entered.

Is the Lord not in Zion, or is her king not in her? Either the Lord himself is the king, or else 'Lord' refers to the Father, 'king' to the Son, according to that which is written under the name of Solomon: O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the son of the king. But why the voice of crying is in Jerusalem and the crying itself comes from a land far off, the cause is manifest: because the Lord is not in her and her king has withdrawn from her.

Why then have they provoked me to anger with their graven images and with foreign vanities? 'But the Lord has withdrawn from them,' he says, 'because they provoked me, who was their Lord and king, to anger by the worship of idols'.

8:20.t: The harvest is past, the summer is ended; and we are not saved. Again the people speaks, which was shut up in Jerusalem by a long siege, saying that the seasons have changed and the circle of the year has rolled round, and all their hope has been made void and has passed away.

8:21.t: Over the breaking of the daughter of my people I am broken and saddened, astonishment has taken hold of me. God answers that in the affliction of Jerusalem he himself appears afflicted, and, after the likeness of a man, he is broken by astonishment.

8:22.t: Let no one, then, run down the law, as if, on account of the penalty, it were not beautiful and good. Shouldn't he who drives away bodily disease appear as a benefactor? Shouldn't he who attempts to deliver the soul from iniquity even more appear as a friend since the soul is a more precious thing than the body? Besides, for the sake of bodily health we submit to incisions, cauterization and medicinal draughts. He who administers them is called savior and healer. He is called this even though he amputates parts, but he works not from a grudge or ill will toward the patient. He instead acts according to the principles that the art prescribes so that the sound parts may not perish along with them. No one accuses the physician's art of wickedness. In the same way, shouldn't we submit, for the soul's sake, to either banishment, or punishment or bonds, as long as from unrighteousness we shall obtain righteousness?

And just as in the one case we put up with operations and cauterisings and the taking of bitter drugs for the treatment of the body, so also in this case we must receive the cutting effects of words of rebuke and the bitter drugs of blame for the cure of the soul. This is what the prophetic word says by way of rebuke to those who have not received correction: “Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why has not the healing of the daughter of my people gone up?”

In such a state of things as this, “Shall they fall and not arise? Shall he turn away and not return?” Why did the virgin turn shamefully away, though she had heard Christ her bridegroom saying through the mouth of Jeremiah, “And I said, after she had done all these things (committed all these fornications, LXX.), turn thou unto me, but she returned not?” “Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there? Why then is not the health of the daughter of my people recovered?” You might indeed find many remedies for evil in Scripture, many medicines to save from destruction and lead to health; the mysteries of death and resurrection, the sentences of terrible judgment and everlasting punishment; the doctrines of repentance and of remission of sins; all the countless illustrations of conversion, the piece of money, the sheep, the son who wasted his substance with harlots, who was lost and was found, who was dead and alive again. Let us not use these remedies for ill; by these means let us heal our soul.

Is there no resin in Gilead, or is there no physician there? Why then has the scar of the daughter of my people not closed over? Not only in the present passage, but also in many other testimonies of the Scriptures we find the resin of Gilead put for repentance and medicine; and we find that God now wonders why the wounds of Jerusalem have by no means been healed and the scars have not yet drawn over the skin, because there are no prophets or priests by whose medicine they ought to be healed.

9:1.t: Now is the time to quote the words of the prophet and to say, “Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people.” Though they are wrapped in profound silence and lie stunned by their misfortune, robbed of all sense of feeling by the fatal blow, I at all events must not let such a fall go unlamented. If, to Jeremiah, it seemed that those whose bodies had been wounded in war, were worthy of innumerable lamentations, what shall be said of such a disaster of souls? “My slain men,” it is said, “are not slain with the sword, nor dead in battle.” But I am bewailing the sting of the real death, the grievousness of sin and the fiery darts of the wicked one, which have savagely set on fire souls as well as bodies.

Who will give water to my head, and to my eyes a fountain of tears? And I will weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people. 'If I,' he says, 'were turned wholly into weeping, and there were not drops of tears at all but the abundance of a river, still I could not worthily weep for the slain of the daughter of my people. For so great are the evils that by their greatness they surpass all grief over them'. And this can be understood as much from the person of the prophet as from that of the Lord.

Isaac: Not every kind of shedding of tears is produced by one feeling or one virtue. For in one way does that weeping originate which is caused by the pricks of our sins smiting our heart, of which we read: "I have laboured in my groanings, every night I will wash my bed; I will water my couch with my tears." And again: "Let tears run down like a torrent day and night: give thyself no rest, and let not the apple of thine eye cease." In another, that which arises from the contemplation of eternal good things and the desire of that future glory, owing to which even richer well-springs of tears burst forth from uncontrollable delights and boundless exultation, while our soul is athirst for the mighty Living God, saying, "When shall I come and appear before the presence of God? My tears have been my meat day and night," declaring with daily crying and lamentation: "Woe is me that my sojourning is prolonged;" and: "Too long hath my soul been a sojourner." […]
9:1.s: The First Conference of Abbot Isaac, Chapter 29

9:2.t: The unrighteous man then, in every respect corrupts his body; stealing, committing adultery, cursing, being drunken, and doing such like things. Even as Jeremiah, the prophet, convicts Israel of these things, crying out and saying, ‘Oh, that I had a lodge far off in the wilderness! then would I leave my people and depart from them: for they are all adulterers, an assembly of oppressors, who draw out their tongue as a bow; lying and not truth has prevailed upon the earth, and they proceed from iniquities to iniquities; but Me they have not known.’ Thus, for wickedness and falsehood, and for deeds, in which they [proceed] from iniquity to iniquity, he reproves their practices; but, because they knew not the Lord, and were faithless, he charges them with unrighteousness.

Who will give me in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfarers? And I will forsake my people and withdraw from them. LXX: who would give me in the wilderness a last dwelling, that I may leave my people and withdraw from them? 'It is better,' he says, 'to dwell in the farthest wilderness than to abide among such great crimes of men'. Hence the Savior also said in the Gospel: how long shall I bear with you? And in another place it is written: at that time he who understands shall sit and be silent, for it is a most evil time.

For they are all adulterers, an assembly of transgressors, and they have stretched out their tongue like a bow of falsehood and not of truth; they have grown strong in the land, for they have gone forth from evil to evil, and they have not known me, says the Lord. Sinners pass from evil to evil when they exchange idol for idol and go over from sins to sins, or at any rate pass from the evil of the siege to captivity. And of the saints indeed it is said: they shall go from strength to strength, but of sinners: they have gone forth from evil to evil. And the cause of all their miseries is that they did not know the Lord, and that it is an assembly of men transgressing and arming their tongue like a stretched bow for blasphemy; and they have grown strong in the land, so that they deserve to hear: earth you are and into earth you shall go.

9:4.t: Let each one guard himself from his neighbor, and let him not have confidence in any brother of his, for every brother supplants with supplanting, and every friend walks deceitfully, and a man will mock his brother, and they will not speak the truth; for their tongue has learned to speak falsehood — or for they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood —. They have labored to act wickedly — or they have acted wickedly and have not ceased, so as to be converted —. Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit; in deceit — or usury upon usury and deceit in deceit; — they have refused — or they would not — to know me, says the Lord. This passage is to be used in a time of persecution and distress, when faith is either rare or none, when neither brother nor neighbor is to be trusted and his enemies are those of his household, when, according to the Gospel, the father will hand over the son and the son the father, and two are divided against three and three against two.

9:5.t: And what he adds: they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood or their tongue has learned to speak falsehood, shows that the habit of lying is in a manner turned into nature, and that they act with zeal so as to do wicked things.

What are we to do with such a useful member? From it we pray to God, we confess our sins, we give praise, we sing to God with one voice in harmony, and in our daily lives, we either show mercy when we converse with others, or we give counsel. What are we to do now? Our very tongue offers you service. What are we to do so that we do not sin with our tongue? Especially since it has been said: "Death and life are in the power of the tongue," and again it has been said: "I have seen many fall by the edge of the sword, but not as many as by the tongue." Again it has been said: "The tongue is a small member, yet it boasts of great things. Consider how a great forest is set on fire by a small spark." Again the same Lord said: "They have taught their tongue to speak lies." Oh, they have taught it! For habit causes it to speak lies; even if you do not wish to, it speaks lies. […]

For what sinner defiles himself unwillingly by adulteries and fornication? Who against his will prepares plots against his neighbour? Who is driven by unavoidable necessity to oppress a man by false witness or cheat him by theft, or covet the goods of another or shed his blood? Nay rather, as Scripture says, "Mankind is diligently inclined to wickedness from his youth." For to such an extent are all inflamed by the love of sin and desire to carry out what they like, that they actually look out with watchful care for an opportunity of committing wickedness and are afraid of being too slow to enjoy their lusts, and glory in their shame and the mass of their crimes, as the Apostle says in censure, and seek credit for themselves out of their own confusion, of whom also the prophet Jeremiah maintains that they commit their flagitious crimes not only not unwillingly nor with ease of heart and body, but with laborious efforts to such an extent that they come to toil to carry them out, so that they are prevented even by the […]
9:5.s: The Third Conference of Abbot Theonas, Chapter 1

9:5.t: The insincere are to be admonished to learn how heavy is the labor of deception. They endure it with guilt. They are afraid of being found out. They are ever seeking dishonest defenses. They are agitated by fearful suspicions. But there is nothing safer to defend than sincerity, nothing easier to say than truth. For, when obliged to defend its deceit, the heart is wearied with hard labor. For it is written, "The labor of their own lips shall cover them." For what now fills them then covers them, since it then presses down with sharp retribution one whose soul it now elevates with a mild uneasiness. It is said through Jeremiah, "They have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity." Said more plainly: "They who might have been friends of truth without labor, labor to sin."
9:5.s: The Book of Pastoral Rule, Part III, Chapter XI

9:6.t: And as for what follows: your dwelling is in the midst of deceit, in deceit, the word is properly directed to the prophet, that he dwells in the midst of a lying people — or, as the Seventy translated: usury upon usury and deceit upon deceit — and that they daily increase their crimes and by no means repent of their former deed, but heap new crimes upon past ones; doing these things, they act with all eagerness so as not to know the Lord, who commanded that these things should not be done.

9:7.t: Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will melt — or I will test by fire — and try them; for what else shall I do in the face of the daughter of my people? Or for I will act in the face of the wickedness of the daughter of my people. Whenever we are subject to distresses, we receive evils from God and are tested by persecutions, so that whatever adulterated matter is in us may be smelted out by the heat of tribulations and miseries: for the silver of the Lord is tested by fire, proved in the earth, purified sevenfold.

9:8.t: Their tongue is a wounding arrow, it has spoken deceit; with his mouth he speaks peace with his friend and secretly lays snares for him. Shall I not visit upon these things, says the Lord, or on such a nation shall my soul not take vengeance? Every heretic who wounds the hearts of his hearers, of those who do not know what is written: keep your heart with all watchfulness, possesses a wounding arrow and speaks in deceit, and while with his mouth he promises peace to his neighbor, he secretly sets snares.

9:9.t: As for the following verses, in which he says: shall I not visit upon these things, says the Lord, or on such a nation shall my soul not take vengeance? He makes frequent use of them in this prophet, so that, when he has enumerated the evil works one by one, he infers that he does justly what he does.

9:10.t: Upon the mountains I will take up — or take up — weeping and lamentation, and over the beautiful places — or the paths — of the desert a wailing, because they are burned up — or they have failed — because there is no man — or human being — passing through. And they have not heard the voice of the possessor — or of substance —; from the bird of the heaven to the beasts they have migrated and withdrawn. When the Babylonian comes upon them and lays everything waste, the desolation of the province is prophesied: that there is wailing on the mountains, weeping in the desert or in the paths of the wilderness, that all things have failed and been burned up, and there is no one to walk through the land, all having been slain, and nothing has remained that can breathe and live. Hence for 'possessor' the Seventy translated 'of substance', which in Hebrew is called 'macne'; and 'substance' here is not taken for ousia, that is, 'essence', but for 'wealth' and 'riches'. […]

9:11.t: And I will give Jerusalem into heaps of sand — or into exile — and into lairs of dragons, and the cities of Judah I will give into desolation, because there is no inhabitant. When churchmen and all the teachers have failed, then Jerusalem is given into exile or into heaps of sand, so that heretical speech prevails in her and she is made a lair of dragons and her cities are reduced to a wilderness, and there is in her no dwelling of the divine word and of him who says: I will dwell and walk among them, and I will be their God.

9:12.t: Who is the wise man who may understand this, and to whom the word of the mouth of the Lord may come, and who may declare it: why the land has perished and is burned up like a desert, because there is none who passes through? And the Lord said: Because they have forsaken my law, which I gave them, and have not heard my voice and have not walked in it, and have gone after the perversity of their heart and after the Baals, whom they learned from their fathers. The prophet asks whether he can find anyone of the wise in Jerusalem, and of those to whom the word of God comes and who can declare the will of the Lord and give the reasons why Judea has been reduced to a wilderness and, all having been slain, no one has remained to pass through it.

9:13.t: And he brings in the Lord answering and giving the reasons: because they had forsaken his law, which he had given them, and had not heard his voice nor done what had been commanded, but had gone after the perversity of their heart. Therefore we must trust not in our own will but in the Lord; for the heart in men is perverse, and from our heart come forth the worst thoughts. And after the Baals, he says, they have gone, whom they learned from their fathers. Bahal is the idol of the Sidonians and is of the singular number, but Bahalim of the plural number. Therefore neither the error of parents nor that of ancestors is to be followed, but the authority of the Scriptures and the command of God who teaches.

9:15.t: Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will feed them, this people, with wormwood — or with distresses — and I will give them water of gall for drink, and I will scatter them among the nations which neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until they are consumed. This can be prophesied both of the near time, when they were taken captive by the Chaldeans, and properly of this present time, when they have been scattered among the nations which neither they nor their fathers had known, and, divided through the whole world, have been fed with wormwood, or with necessities and distresses. And they have received water of gall for drink, which either signifies the greatness of their evils and the everlasting yoke of captivity, or else means that, through ignorance of the law of God, they are going to receive Antichrist instead of Christ. […]

9:17.t: It is our part too henceforth to mourn, or rather we have need to say this every day. We profit nothing by our prayers, nothing by our advice and exhortation, it remaineth therefore that we weep. Thus did Christ; after having many times exhorted those in Jerusalem, when they profited nothing, He wept at their hardness. This also do the Prophets, and this let us do now. Henceforth is the season for mourning and tears and wailing; it is seasonable for us also to say now, "Call for the mourning women, and send for the cunning women, that they may cry aloud" (Jer. ix. 17); perhaps thus we shall be able to cast out the malady of those who build splendid houses, of those who surround themselves with lands gotten by rapine.
9:17.s: Homily on the Gospel of John 64

9:17.t: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Consider — or understand — and call the mourning women, and let them come, and send to those who are wise, and let them hasten — or let them speak —, let them make haste and take up a lamentation over us — or over you — and let our eyes — or your — bring down tears and our eyelids — or your — flow with waters, for a voice of lamentation has been heard from Zion or in Zion. On account of the coming captivity and overthrow of Jerusalem he bids the mourning women be called, who in times of grief are accustomed, with a tearful voice and beating their arms with their hands, to provoke the people to tears; for this custom remains to this day in Judea, that women with hair loosened and breasts bared, with a measured chant, stir everyone to weeping. And God joins himself to them with the feeling of one who suffers with them, or the prophet does, so as to say that whatever the people endures, he himself endures and feels. […]

9:19.t: How are we laid waste and confounded exceedingly? Because we have forsaken the land, for our tents have been thrown down — or we have cast away —. This is the voice of those lamenting Zion: how are we laid waste and confounded exceedingly? And at once they answer themselves and set out the causes of the devastation, saying: because we have forsaken the land through our own fault and sin, and our tents have been thrown down, which they once possessed as if passing by. Let the crowds of those who once believed say this too in persecution: that they have been laid waste and confounded for this reason, because they have forsaken the land of the Lord and deserted their tents.

9:20.t: Hear therefore, O women, the word of the Lord, and let your ear take up the speech of his mouth, and teach your daughters lamentation, and each woman her neighbor wailing, for death has come up through our windows, it has entered our houses, to destroy the little ones from outside, the young men from the streets! In the preceding section he had said: call the mourning women, and let them come, and send to those who are wise, and let them hasten; now he speaks as if to women present, to the condemnation of the priests and teachers and of all the men, so that, since these cease from teaching, the women may hear the word of the Lord and take up the words of his mouth and teach their daughters and their neighbors wailing and the causes of tears, for death, he says, has come up through our windows, it has entered our houses. […]

9:21.t: One window is one sense: through this the bridegroom looks. Another window is another sense: and through this too the bridegroom carefully gazes. For through what senses does the word of God not look? But what it is to look through the windows, and how the bridegroom gazes through them, the following example will teach. Where the bridegroom does not look, there death is found climbing up, as we read in Jeremiah: Behold, death has climbed up through your windows. When you have looked upon a woman to lust after her, already death has climbed up through your windows.
9:21.s: HOMILIES ON THE SONG OF SONGS, HOMILY 2

9:21.t: But we may understand the windows to be the bodily senses, through which either death or life enters into the soul; for so does it signify when the prophet Jeremiah speaks concerning sinners, saying: "Death has climbed up through your windows." How does death climb up through the windows? If the eyes of a sinner should look upon a woman, and he should commit adultery with her in his heart, thus death has entered into the soul through the windows of the eyes.
9:21.s: COMMENTARY ON THE SONG OF SONGS, BOOK 3

9:21.t: The first point to be considered is—What is this great rivalry of speech and endless talking? What is this new disease of insatiability? Why have we tied our hands and armed our tongues? We do not praise either hospitality, or brotherly love, or conjugal affection, or virginity; nor do we admire liberality to the poor, or the chanting of Psalms, or nightlong vigils, or tears. We do not keep under the body by fasting, or go forth to God by prayer; nor do we subject the worse to the better—I mean the dust to the spirit—as they would do who form a just judgment of our composite nature; we do not make our life a preparation for death; nor do we make ourselves masters of our passions, mindful of our heavenly nobility; […]

These are the windows of which Jeremiah also says: Death has entered through our windows; for the enemies desire to enter through all our senses, and to take the city of a good conscience, and to run about through our fortifications, and to destroy the houses which we have built for ourselves by good works. And they do all things entering through the windows like a thief, for they do not enter openly, that they may shoot in the dark at the upright of heart.

For Jeremiah says: 'Death has entered through your windows.' Now we have five windows: that is, sight, hearing, taste, smell, and touch. If therefore I have looked at a woman to lust after her, I have already committed adultery with her in my heart; and death has entered through my window, that is, through sight. If the lyre or the organ or the reed-pipe as it were dissolves me, death has entered through my hearing. But if I touch something soft, and am unstrung by the softness of the body, death has entered through my touch, and the rest likewise.

9:22.t: Speak: Thus says the Lord: And the carcass of man shall fall — or the corpses of men — like dung upon the face of the region — or of the field — and like hay behind the back of the reaper, and there is none who gathers. The Hebrew word that is written with three letters, 'daleth, beth, res' — for it has no vowels in the middle —, if it is read, according to the context and the judgment of the reader, as 'dabar', means 'word'; if as 'deber', 'death'; if as 'dabber', 'speak'. Hence the Seventy and Theodotion joined it to the previous section, so as to say: to destroy the little ones from outside, the young men from the streets, by death. But Aquila and Symmachus translated lalēson, 'speak', so that God commands the prophet to speak what follows: thus says the Lord and the rest. […]

9:23.t: Let us therefore, brethren, be of humble mind, laying aside all haughtiness, and pride, and foolishness, and angry feelings; and let us act according to that which is written (for the Holy Spirit saith, "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, neither let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him that glorieth glory in the Lord, in diligently seeking Him, and doing judgment and righteousness"), being especially mindful of the words of the Lord Jesus which He spake, teaching us meekness and long-suffering. For thus He spoke: "Be ye merciful, that ye may obtain mercy; forgive, that it may be forgiven to you; as ye do, so shall it be done unto you; as ye judge, so shall ye be judged; as ye are kind, so shall kindness be shown to you; with what measure ye mete, with the same it shall be measured to you." By this precept and by these rules let us establish ourselves, that we walk with all humility in obedience to His holy words. […]
9:23.s: Clement's First Letter to the Corinthians, Chapter 13

9:23.t: Let us therefore, brethren, be of humble mind, laying aside all haughtiness, and pride, and foolishness, and angry feelings; and let us act according to that which is written (for the Holy Spirit saith, "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, neither let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him that glorieth glory in the Lord, in diligently seeking Him, and doing judgment and righteousness"), being especially mindful of the words of the Lord Jesus which He spake, teaching us meekness and long-suffering. For thus He spoke: "Be ye merciful, that ye may obtain mercy; forgive, that it may be forgiven to you; as ye do, so shall it be done unto you; as ye judge, so shall ye be judged; as ye are kind, so shall kindness be shown to you; with what measure ye mete, with the same it shall be measured to you."

What is the philosophy that the apostle bids us shun? This, then, "the wisdom of the world is foolishness with God." "The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain." Let no one therefore glory on account of pre-eminence in human thought. For it is written well in Jeremiah, "Let not the wise person glory in his wisdom, and let not the mighty person glory in his might, and let not the rich person glory in his riches. But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows that I am the Lord, that executes mercy and judgment and righteousness on the earth: for in these things is my delight, say the Lord."

We must trust in God only, and in him we must glory. In Jeremiah: "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the strong man glory in his strength, nor let the rich man glory in his riches. But let him that glories glory in this, that he understands and knows that I am the Lord, who does mercy, and judgment, and righteousness upon the earth, because in them is my pleasure, says the Lord."
9:23.s: Treatise XII. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews 3:10

9:23.t: Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, and let not the strong man glory in his strength, and let not the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this: to know — or to understand — and to know me, that I am the Lord, who do mercy and judgment and righteousness on the earth! For these things please me — or for in these is my will —, says the Lord. All the pride of men is taken away, while their wisdom and strength and wealth are reckoned as nothing, and this is the only glorying: that one should know and understand that he himself is the Lord, who does mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth; that all things are governed by the providence and righteousness of God, and that the things which seem to us to have no reason are full of righteousness and reason. For these things alone please God, and in these is his will. […]

If you glory in wisdom, by that very fact you lose wisdom. "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, and let not the strong man glory in his strength." And the cause of this is given in Ezekiel, where it is said: "You, full of wisdom and beauty, were in the delights of the paradise of God: you lost your wisdom on account of your beauty."

9:24.t: So that, as it is written: Let him who glories, glory in the Lord. This is written in the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 9:24). Worthy is what the prophet says, that we should glory in God; because he who glories in the Lord will not be able to be confounded; for his works and his magnificence appear in the things he has done. And therefore, he says, let them be confounded in their idols, which do not send rain and did not make heaven and earth: in like manner also those who glory in men, whom they surely know to be of no power; wherefore Scripture also says: Vain is hope in man (Jer. 17:5).

Forasmuch then as our turning away from God is our own act, and this is evil will; but our turning to God is not possible, except He rouses and helps us, and this is good will,—what have we that we have not received?
