12:14.t: And as to what he adds: against all my most wicked neighbors: according to the letter, the neighbors of the holy land are the Edomites, the Philistines, Moab and Ammon; but according to tropology, they are all the heretics, who are reckoned under the name of Christ and are neighbors rather than inhabitants of the holy land, who touch the inheritance of God and lay it waste; and it is said of them that they are removed from the midst of the land and that the house of Judah is taken out of their midst. These, when they have been plucked up and freed from the jaws of the heretics, will obtain the mercy of God and will be brought back into their inheritance and into their land.

12:16.t: And it shall be, if, being instructed, they learn the ways of my people, so as to swear in my name: The Lord lives, as they taught my people to swear by Baal, they shall be built up in the midst of my people; but if they do not hear, I will pluck up that nation with plucking up and destruction, says the Lord. If those brought over from heresy into the Church learn the ways of the people of God and swear in the name of the Lord, and not in the name of the idols which they fashioned out of their own heart, they will be built up by the Lord and will be part of his people. But if, having been brought over into the Church, they keep remnants of perverse dogmas and do not hear the words of the Lord, that nation will be plucked up from the midst of the people of God with a perpetual plucking up and destruction, so that no place of repentance whatever is left to them. […]

13:1.t: The blessed John disdained sheep's wool because it savored of luxury; he preferred camel's hair and clothed himself in it, giving us an example of simple, frugal living. Incidentally, he also ate only honey and locusts, food that is sweet and with a spiritual significance. So it was that he prepared the way of the Lord and kept it humble and chaste. He fled from the false pretenses of the city and led a peaceful life in the desert with God, away from all vanity, boasting and servitude. How could he possibly have worn a purple mantle? Elijah used a sheepskin for his garment and girded it tight with a belt made of leather. Isaiah, another historic prophet, went "naked and without sandals" and often put on sackcloth as a garment of humility. If you protest and make mention of Jeremiah, he wore only a loincloth made of linen.

After these things let us look at what concerns the loincloth. For "Thus," it says, "says the Lord: Go and acquire for yourself a linen loincloth, and put it around your loins, and do not pass it through water. And I acquired a loincloth according to the word of the Lord and put it around my loins. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Take the loincloth that is around your loins, and arise and go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in the cleft of the rock." After some days he comes there, and finds this loincloth rotted through. And the Lord adds to it, giving the occasion for the interpretation of the loincloth, saying: "Just as the loincloth clings to the loins of a man, so did I cause the house of Israel and the whole house of Judah to cling to myself, says the Lord, that they might become for me a renowned people and a boast and a glory, and they did not listen to me." Therefore the prophet is taken up in the place of God, girding around his loins the linen loincloth, as God girds the people; […]

Yet such is the order of nature. While truth is always bitter, pleasantness waits upon evildoing. Isaiah goes naked without blushing, as a type of the captivity to come. Jeremiah is sent from Jerusalem to the Euphrates (a river in Mesopotamia) and leaves his girdle to be marred in the Chaldaean camp, among the Assyrians hostile to his people. Ezekiel is told to eat bread made of mingled seeds and baked over the dung of people and cattle. He is commanded to experience the death of his wife without shedding a tear. Amos is driven from Samaria. Why is he driven from it? Surely in this case, as in the others, because he was a spiritual surgeon who cut away the parts diseased by sin and urged people to repentance. The apostle Paul says, "Am I therefore become your enemy because I tell you the truth?" And so the Savior found it, from whom many of the disciples turned back from following him because his sayings seemed hard.

Thus says the Lord to me: Go and get yourself a loincloth — or girdle — of linen, and you shall put it upon your loins, and you shall not bring it into water — or it shall not pass through water —! And I got the loincloth according to the word of the Lord and put it about my loins. And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying: Take the loincloth — or girdle —, which you have got, which is about your loins, and arise, go to the Euphrates and hide it there in a cleft of the rock! And I went and hid it in the Euphrates, as the Lord had commanded me. And it came to pass after very many days, the Lord said to me: Arise, go to the Euphrates and take from there the loincloth — or girdle —, which I commanded you to hide there! And I went to the Euphrates and dug and took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it; and behold, the loincloth — or girdle — had rotted, so that it was fit for no use. […]

The Lord has reigned, and he has clothed himself with the patriarchs and the prophets and the believing people. He has clothed himself in beauty: the patriarchs and the prophets were as it were the garment of Christ. That is the loincloth which is written of in Jeremiah: that is the loincloth which Jeremiah had about his loins. Do you wish to know that the saints are, as it were, a loincloth, the garment of God? Afterwards God himself speaks to Jeremiah: 'Just as you,' he says, 'placed that loincloth about your loins, so I too have joined my people to myself.' As, then, a garment is about a man, so the people is about God. But because this loincloth, because this beauty with which the Lord had been clothed, was exposed across the Euphrates in a cleft of the rock, and there rotted away, and was led off into captivity by the Assyrians—what does the Lord do? […]

Do you wish to know how we clothe the Lord? We read in Jeremiah: 'Take unto thee, he says, a girdle, and go, he says, to the Euphrates, and put it in a hole of the rock. And I did, he says, what the Lord had commanded me. And after some days I returned to the Euphrates, and behold, he says, the girdle had rotted, so that it was fit for no use. And the Lord spoke, he says, to me'. Attentively take heed. 'As, he says, thou hadst a girdle about thy loins, so also I had this people about me, saith the Lord'. Why have I said all this? To show that believers are the garment of Christ.

13:12.t: What the prophet is commanded by God to say ought to be worthy of God, [yet] it appears that it is not worthy of God so long as we remain at the level of the letter, so that someone else, on hearing the letter, might say: "These letters are folly." But it is the unspiritual man (psychikos) who will say this; for "the unspiritual man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are folly to him." Look, then, at what the wording says: "And you shall say to this people: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel" — what "the Lord, the God of Israel" says, let it be worthy of the Lord, the God of Israel — "Every wineskin shall be filled with wine. And it shall be, if they say to you: Do we not surely know that every wineskin shall be filled with wine?" And those who answer, if they take their stand on the literal statement and say these things, claiming to have known that "every wineskin shall be filled with wine," are lying. For it is not the case that "every wineskin shall be filled with wine." […]

And these things He said, setting laws and rules for His own disciples, that when they should have to receive as disciples those of all sorts that should come from the whole world, they might deal with them very gently. "Neither do men put new wine into old bottles." Seest thou His illustrations, how like the Old Testament? the garment? the wine skins? For Jeremiah too calls the people "a girdle," and makes mention again of "bottles" and of "wine." Thus, the discourse being about gluttony and a table, He takes His illustrations from the same.
13:12.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 30:5

13:12.t: You shall say therefore to them — or to the people — this word: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Every flask — or wineskin — shall be filled with wine. And they will say to you: Do we not know that every flask — or wineskin — is filled with wine? And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, and the kings who sit of the stock — or the sons — of David upon his throne, and the priests and the prophets and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with drunkenness, and I will scatter them, a man from his brother, and fathers and sons together, says the Lord; I will not spare — or I will not long for — and I will not yield nor have mercy, so as not to destroy them. The Hebrew word 'nebel' Aquila's first edition translated 'flask', the second 'nebel' itself, Symmachus 'mixing-bowl', the Seventy 'wineskin', Theodotion 'vessel'; […]

13:13.t: Then he teaches, on account of those who had sinned — as far as the literal sense goes — in Jerusalem at that time and in Judea, with what sort of wine God is about to fill these wineskins, the sinners. For it is written: "If they say to you: Do we not surely know that every wineskin shall be filled with wine? then you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I fill all the inhabitants of this land, and the kings who sit as sons of David upon his throne, and the priests." He who is about to punish spares no one. Not because someone bore the title of prophet, yet has sins, will he not be filled with the threats that are spoken. Not because someone bore the title of priest and seemed to hold the preeminence of a more honorable name among the people does God spare him, so that he should not be punished when he has sinned. But the things recorded concerning those people, the apostle says, were written for our sake, "upon whom the ends of the ages have come." […]

13:14.t:
"And the priests," then, "and the prophets and Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem" God says he will fill "with drunkenness" and will scatter "them, a man and his brother, and their fathers and their sons." And let us understand these things also thus: the righteous God gathers together, but the sinners he scatters. For this reason, at the time when men did not move from the east, God did not scatter them; but when they moved "from the east" and "a man said to his neighbor: Come, and let us build for ourselves a city and a tower, whose top shall be up to heaven," God says concerning these: "Come, and going down let us confound their language there," and each one is confounded and is scattered to some place of the earth. And the people of Israel too, so long as they did not sin, were in Judea, but when they sinned they are scattered thereafter from the inhabited world and dispersed everywhere.

Understand something of this sort for me concerning all of us as well. […]

13:15.t: Now that the one section has been circumscribed, let us see also what the other teaches us: "Hear and give ear, and be not lifted up, for the Lord has spoken. Give glory to the Lord our God before it grows dark, and before your feet stumble upon dark mountains; and you will wait for light, and there will be a shadow of death there, and they will be set in darkness. But if you do not hear secretly, your soul will weep before the face of insolence, and your eyes will bring down tears, because the flock of the Lord has been crushed." He wishes these same people to hear and to give ear, being satisfied neither with their merely hearing nor with their merely giving ear. Therefore he says: "Hear and give ear." Then, after this, he commands them not to be lifted up, and teaches what must be done. What, then, is "to hear" and what is "to give ear," let us consider from the very wording. […]

Hear and perceive with your ears, do not be lifted up, for the Lord has spoken! Because he had said above: Every wineskin shall be filled with wine, so that the kings too and the priests and the prophets and every inhabitant of Jerusalem should be filled with drunkenness, therefore he joins on and says: Hear and perceive with your ears, as much outwardly as inwardly, as much with the mind as with the body, and do not be lifted up through pride, considering your frailty and that there is no one who, according to the quality of sin, is free of this drunkenness. Hence he who lifts himself up against him through pride is destroyed and corrupted and is unworthy of the mercy of God.

13:16.t:
And let us see also what he bids us do after these things: "Give," he says, "to the Lord our God glory before it grows dark, before your feet stumble upon dark mountains; and you will wait for light." He wishes the one who gives "glory to God" to give "glory to God" while there is light, since the glory of God cannot be proclaimed once it has grown dark and darkness has come. When, then, does it grow dark, and when does the darkening not occur? "Work while the light is in you." "The light is in" you if you have in you the one who said: "I am the light of the world." As long as this rises for you, glorify God; but know that a certain darkening can occur, and one must not let this darkening remain, but must give glory to God before it grows dark.

Perhaps we shall understand what is written by using an evangelical saying spoken by the Savior which runs thus: "Work while it is day; night comes when no one is able to work." He named there this present age "day" (but I necessarily added the "there"; […]

Give glory to the Lord our God, before it grows dark and before your feet stumble upon the misty — or dark — mountains! You will wait for light, and there will be the shadow of death, and they will be placed in darkness — or, according to the Hebrew: and he will set it in the shadow of death and in gloom —. But if you do not hear, in secret the soul will weep, mine — or yours — before the face of pride or injury. Those to whom the divine word had said: Hear and perceive with your ears and do not be lifted up, he now calls to repentance, that, before they are led to Babylon and their feet stumble upon the dark or misty mountains, they should give glory to God. Hence sinners too are often told: Give glory to God! And that Babylon and the whole region of the Chaldeans are called misty or dark mountains we read at the beginning of Isaiah, against Babylon, where it is written: Upon the misty mountain lift up a sign, which in Hebrew is called 'neseptha'. […]

'But if', he says, 'you refuse to hear me, secretly' — according to Aquila 'in darkness' — 'the soul will weep, mine' — or, according to the Seventy, 'yours' — 'before the face of pride, so that not even groaning and weeping may be free, lest the eyes of the victors be offended'. But we can also interpret this passage thus: the Savior speaks: 'Work while it is day; the night will come, when no one can work any longer'. Of this time there is also the prophecy of Isaiah: For the stars of heaven and Orion and all the adornment of heaven will not give light, and they will be darkened at the rising of the sun, and the moon will not give light. Zephaniah too agrees in the same words, saying: A day of tribulation and distress, a day of misery and perdition, a day of darkness and whirlwind, a day of cloud and gloom. […]

13:17.t: "But if you do not hear in secret, your soul shall weep before the face of insolence." Of those who hear, some hear in secret, but others, even if they hear, do not hear in secret. What then is it to hear in secret, other than "but we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, the hidden wisdom, which God foreordained before the ages for our glory"? And again elsewhere it is said that "the greater part of the works of God are in hidden things." If I hear the law, either I hear in secret or I do not hear in secret. The Jew does not hear the law in secret; therefore he is circumcised openly, not knowing that "the Jew is not the one in the open, nor is circumcision that which is in the open in the flesh." But he who hears about circumcision in secret shall be circumcised in what is hidden; […]

Weeping, Jerusalem shall weep — or weeping, it shall weep — and my eye shall shed a tear, and I cannot conceal my grief in silent groans; but the whole cause of the torments is that the flock of the Lord has been taken captive. Let us say to the Jews and to our own Judaizers, who follow only the simple and killing history: Unless you hear secretly, that is, in mystery or in darkness, which God has made his hiding place, and, according to Solomon, so as to understand a parable and a dark saying, the soul will weep, the prophet's or their own, before the face of pride, while through contumacy they resist God. Hence there will also be continual weeping and perpetual tears, because the flock of the Lord has been taken captive and corrupted by the true Nebuchadnezzar.

13:18.t: Say to the king and to the mistress — or say to the king and to the mighty —: Humble yourselves, sit down, for there has come down — or there has been taken away — from your head the crown of your glory! The cities of the south are shut up, and there is none who opens; all Judea has been carried away — or all Judah has been carried away — with exile complete — or captivity —. The prophet is commanded to speak to King Jeconiah and to his mother, whom he calls lady and mistress or queen, that they should humble themselves and sit in the dust; for they have lost the royal dignity and are to be handed over to the Babylonian king.

The cities of the south are shut up, that is, the tribe of Judah and Jerusalem, which, lying next to the desert, faces toward the south, and there is none who opens them, surrounded as they are by siege. All Judea has been carried away — or all Judah — with exile complete, or 'it has received what it deserved, and it has been fulfilled in it'; for so the Seventy translated. He raves in this place who understands the king as Christ and the mighty as angels or apostles, as if they were to take on the body of humility and sit in the dust and lose — either the king or the mighty — from their head the crown and the glory of strength. He also interprets the shut cities of the south as hell, as cities opened to no one, and says that all the glory of Judah was carried away when there was fulfilled in the passion: All have turned aside, together they have become useless; there is none who does good, there is not even one. The Hebrew word 'gebira' Aquila and Symmachus translated 'mistress' and 'lady'; […]

13:20.t: Lift up your eyes and see those who are coming — or you who are coming — from the north! Where is the flock that was given to you, your glorious herd? What will you say when he visits you? For you teach them against yourself and instruct them to your own head. The inhabitants of Jerusalem are commanded to lift up their eyes and see the Chaldeans coming from the region of the north; and the city herself is questioned, and it is said to her: 'Where is the flock that was given to you, your glorious herd? Where is your people, which you had received from God? Where is that multitude, so great and glorious that you would have believed the crowd of a whole province gathered into one place? […]

13:21.t: Will not pains seize you like a woman in labor? But if you say in your heart: Why have these things come upon me? Because of the multitude of your iniquity your more shameful parts have been uncovered, your soles have been polluted — or have been dishonored —. 'While you do not know it, as a sudden childbirth seizes a woman, so a sudden captivity will seize you. But if you wish to complain and ask why you have been handed over to enemies, hear plainly that the multitude of your iniquity has done these things to you, so that, as of a harlot woman whose garments have been lifted, your ignominy has been uncovered and your fornications have been shown in public'. By these things we learn that, so long as sins are lesser, God acts patiently and waits for our repentance; but if we choose to join offenses to offenses and to make a heap of sins, our shameful parts will be uncovered and our soles will be shown to all, either in the present age or in the future. […]

13:23.t: Afterwards he came to Cilicia, and, on meeting with a certain Gelasius, showed him the creed which only an Arian, or a thorough disciple of Arius, could subscribe. Then, indeed, I was yet more confirmed in my alienation from him. I felt that the Ethiopian will never change his skin, nor the leopard his spots, nor a man nurtured in doctrines of perversity ever be able to rub off the stain of his heresy.

Scripture is also not silent about the nature of the leopard. By the varied character of his coat he betrays the variety of his emotions. Jeremias says: ‘If the Ethiopian can change his skin or the leopard his spots.’ This is not said merely of what is external. It refers, also, to changes in the fierce nature of the animal. The Jewish people, whose characters were spoiled because of the gloomy and uneasy fluctuations of their hearts and minds, could not attain the grace of good purpose. Once they had acquired the fierce character of a wild beast, they were unable to return to a better and improved mode of life.

And if, "they could not," is put, instead of, "they would not," do not marvel, for He saith also in another place, "He that is able to receive it, let him receive it." So in many places He is wont to term choice, power... And what saith the Prophet? "If the Ethiopian shall change his skin, or the leopard his spots, this people also shall be able to do good, having learned evil." He saith not that the doing of virtue is impossible to them, but that because they will not, therefore they cannot.
13:23.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 68

13:23.t: By the reading of the prophet the eunuch of Candace, the queen of Ethiopia, is made ready for the baptism of Christ. Though it is against nature, the Ethiopian does change his skin, and the leopard his spots.

Then immediately quickening her pace, she began to move along the old road that leads to Gaza, that is, to the "power" or "wealth" of God, silently meditating on that type of the Gentiles, the Ethiopian eunuch, who, in spite of the prophet, changed his skin and, while he read the Old Testament, found the fountain of the gospel.

If the Ethiopian can change his skin or the leopard its spots, you too will be able to do good, when you have learned evil. This testimony is used against the Church by those who desire to assert diverse natures, and they say that the blackness or the variegation of sins is so great that they cannot pass into whiteness and the beauty of a single color, not attending to what follows: and you will be able to do good, when you have learned evil. For whatever is learned is not of nature but of effort and of one's own will, which through excessive habit and love of sinning is in a manner turned into nature. But this, which is impossible for men, is possible for God: so that it is by no means the Ethiopian and the leopard who are seen to change their nature, but he who works in the Ethiopian and the leopard, as the Apostle says: I can do all things in him who strengthens me, Christ. Hence also in another place: I labored, he says, more than all of them; […]

Chus in the Hebrew tongue is interpreted 'Ethiopian,' that is, black and dark, who has such a soul as he has a body, of whom Jeremiah says: 'If the Ethiopian will change his skin, or the leopard his spots.' So this Chusi signifies his black and Ethiopian enemy, Saul. And he says this: As the Ethiopian cannot change his skin, so this man too cannot change his character. Twice he came into my hands, I could have killed him. Whose blood I could have shed, I wished rather to overcome him by kindness; but his malice cannot be conquered. For just as the Ethiopian's skin cannot be changed, so too his malice cannot be changed.

Also, he showed so much love in his religion that, leaving behind a queen's court, he came from the farthest regions of the world to the Lord's temple. Hence, as a just reward, while he sought the interpretation of something that he was reading, he found Christ, whom he was seeking. Furthermore, as Jerome says, he found the church's font there in the desert, rather than in the golden temple of the synagogue. For there in the desert something happened that Jeremiah declared was to be wondered at, an Ethiopian changed his skin, that is, with the stain of his sins washed away by the waters of baptism, he went up, shining white, to Jesus.

13:24.t: And I will scatter them like stubble that is snatched away by the wind in the desert. This is your lot and the portion of your measure from me, says the Lord or and the portion of your disobedience against me. 'Because through excessive habit of evils they could not change their nature — not by the fault of the Creator, but by the pursuit of ingrained wickedness —, therefore I will scatter them like stubble snatched away by the wind into the wilderness, according to what is written elsewhere: like the dust which the wind casts from the face of the earth'.

13:25.t: And he makes an apostrophe to Jerusalem herself: that this is her lot and this the portion which she herself has chosen, a measure heaped up and full and running over, or the portion of her disobedience, by which she would not acquiesce to the Lord; for with what measure she has measured, it will be measured back to her.

Because you have forgotten me and trusted — or hoped — in falsehood, therefore I too have bared — or will bare and will uncover — your thighs — and hinder parts — before your face, and your ignominy will appear, your adulteries and your neighing, the wickedness — or estrangement — of your fornication. The cause of the scattering of Jerusalem is that she has forgotten God and trusted or hoped in falsehoods. He who, apart from God, trusts in the things of the world forgets God. Hence his thighs or hinder parts are uncovered, so that he may see his own ignominy, and the things that ought to be behind may come to the front, and he himself may perceive what he has done, and his ignominy may appear not only to himself but to all. Your adulteries, he says, and your neighing shows not lust alone but the madness of lust, after the manner of mares that are eager for coupling, as in that line of Vergil: hippomanes, as the shepherds call it by a true name, a sticky venom drips from the groin. […]

13:27.t: Upon the hills in the field I have seen your abominations. Woe to you, Jerusalem! You will not be cleansed — or because you have not been cleansed — after me; how long yet? 'Not only in the midst of the city of Jerusalem but on every hill and in all regions I have seen your idols'; hence it is said to her: 'Woe to you, Jerusalem, because you have not been cleansed after me, so that, though you boasted that you followed my footsteps and paraded the confession of my name, yet you have never been purified, because you have forgotten me and hoped in falsehoods'. Hence he rebukes her and says: How long yet? And the sense is: 'How long shall I wait for you? How long shall I bear it? How long will you forget me to the end and despise my precepts?' He commits fornication on the hills and in the fields and is never cleansed, who, with neck erect through pride, is not humbled under the mighty hand of God but trusts in his own crimes and vices.

14:1.t: The word of the Lord which came to Jeremiah concerning the words of the drought. All things are in accord with the wrath of God; hence the sun also sets at noon upon sinners, and the moon and the other stars do not give their light, and we must suppose that in the time of the siege there were no rains, so that the besieged endured a dearth of water. For the city uses a single spring, that of Siloam, and this not a perennial one, and to the present day a dearth of rains causes a lack not only of crops but also of water to drink.

14:2.t: Judea has mourned — or Judah — and its gates have fallen — or have been made empty — and have been darkened — or have been made dark — upon the earth, and the cry of Jerusalem has gone up. Its elders sent their lesser ones — or younger ones — to the water; they came to draw — or to the wells — and did not find water; they brought back their vessels empty. They were confounded and afflicted — or they blushed — and covered their heads; because of the desolation of the land — or and the works of the land, because they have failed —, because no rain came — or there was no rain — upon the land, the farmers were confounded, they covered their heads. In the time of drought, when the multitude suffers a famine of hearing and learning the word of God, Judea mourns, 'boasting' that it formerly had the worship of God and the 'confession' of the true faith; and its gates are either emptied or fall, which we ought to refer to the senses, through which instruction is conceived by the soul. […]

14:3.t: The elders also, who ought themselves to go to draw the waters, send the younger ones, in whom there are no gray hairs of wisdom, and therefore they come to the wells and do not find the waters which, as the history relates, the patriarchs found. They bring back their vessels empty, the younger ones, that is, not because there were no waters, but because they could not find them. They were confounded and afflicted — or they blushed — and covered their heads — because they could not say with the Apostle: 'But we all, with unveiled face, behold the glory of the Lord' — because of the desolation of the land or and the works of the land have failed, through which we advance to the knowledge of God. And the cause is plain: because no rain came upon the land. For the clouds were commanded not to rain a shower upon it. […]

14:5.t: For the hind also — or the hinds — gave birth in the field — or they gave birth — and forsook — or they forsook —, because there was no grass. And the wild asses stood on the crags, they drew in the wind like dragons; their eyes failed, because there was no grass or hay. Great is the barrenness when even the hinds give birth in the field and forsake their young because there is no grass or hay, so that they, which by the scent of their nostrils draw serpents out of their holes and kill venomous creatures, do not enjoy the food of grace; and when the wild asses also, of which it is written: Who has sent out the wild ass free into the wilderness?, leaving the plains and the open country, stand on the crags and cannot run, and draw in the wind after the likeness of dragons, and their eyes fail and cannot see the clear light, since rational food has been withdrawn. […]

14:7.t: If our iniquities have answered — or have withstood — us, O Lord, act for your name's sake, for many are our turnings away — or our sins —. Against you we have sinned, O expectation of Israel, his Savior in the time of tribulation. If we are in doubt why the rains do not come down upon the land, why all things wither with dryness, let us hear: our iniquities have withstood us; 'therefore, O Lord, not according to our works but according to your holy name, overcome our many turnings away. For against you we have sinned, whom the secrets of the heart do not deceive, and we wait for you, who are the true hope and expectation of Israel and save him in the time of tribulation, according to that which is written: To the Lord I cried when I was in tribulation, and he heard me'. Let us too say, in the time of drought and dearth of waters: 'Against you we have sinned and have done evil before you; we wait for your coming, you who save Israel not by its own merit but by your clemency.'

14:8.t: Why will you be like a settler in the land and like a traveler turning aside to lodge? Why will you be like a wandering man or a mighty one who cannot save? LXX: why have you become like a stranger in the land and like a native turning aside to lodge? Will you be like a man asleep and like a man who cannot save? The Jews understand this passage thus: 'Why do you separate yourself from your people and, like a traveler, for the refreshment of a single hour not care what lodging you use, but, being about to pass on to other places, not save your people and forsake the temple once renowned?' Our people, however, think that it is said of the future dispensation of Christ: that he was to be a pilgrim in the land and to use the hospitality of the earth for a short time, and, like a man passing through and strong, having left Israel, to make for the multitude of the Gentiles, so as to pass from place to place, from people to people, from the temple to the Church.

14:9.t: But what is said according to the Seventy: Will you be like a man asleep and like a man who cannot save? sets down a likeness, not the truth of the matter, according to that which is written: Arise, why do you sleep, O Lord?, not that the Lord sleeps, of whom it is said: He who keeps Israel will not slumber nor sleep, but that he seems to sleep to those whom he forsakes. Finally, in what follows too, it is not written: 'a man asleep', who cannot save, but: 'like a man'; in both, anthrōpopathōs [in human terms].

But you are in us, O Lord, and your name has been invoked upon us; do not forsake us or do not forget us! 'You who among the Jews will be like a stranger and a traveler and a wandering man, forsaking your ancient dwelling, dwell in us, and your name has been invoked upon us, so that we are called Christians; therefore do not forsake us nor forget us, to whom the mouths of all the prophets have sung of your future coming'.

14:10.t: Hence it is that they are always writing, and always altering their own previous statements, and thus they shew an uncertain faith, or rather a manifest unbelief and perverseness. And this, it appears to me, must needs be the case with them; for since, having fallen away from the truth, and desiring to overthrow that sound confession of faith which was drawn up at Nicaea, they have, in the language of Scripture, `loved to wander, and have not refrained their feet;' therefore, like Jerusalem of old, they labour and toil in their changes, sometimes writing one thing, and sometimes another, but only for the sake of gaining time, and that they may continue enemies of Christ, and deceivers of mankind.
14:10.s: LETTER TO THE BISHOPS OF EGYPT 1:6

14:10.t: Thus says the Lord to this people: because it has loved — or they have loved — to move its feet and has not rested — or they have not spared — and it has not pleased the Lord — or and God was not well pleased in them —, now he will remember their iniquities and will visit their sins. When the people says: 'Why have you become like a stranger and a traveler and a wanderer, so as to forsake your dwelling?', the Lord answers the people that was once his own: 'Do you wish to know the reason? Listen to what is said: because the people has loved to move its feet and has not withdrawn them from the fetter of sins, or has not rested and could not stand, therefore I too have forsaken it, and I have no good pleasure in it'. He, then, who long delayed and through patience was unwilling to punish sinners, since they persisted in wickedness, will remember their iniquities and will visit the sins of those who are, as it were, sick and do not perceive God, so that they may cease to sin any more. […]

14:11.t: And the Lord said to me: Do not pray for this people for good! When they fast, I will not hear their prayers, and if they offer burnt offerings and victims, I will not accept them, for by the sword and by famine and by pestilence I will consume them. It is foolish to pray for one who has sinned unto death, as John says: There is a sin unto death; I do not say that one should pray for that. All iniquity is sin, and there is a sin not unto death. Fasts and prayers and victims and burnt offerings profit only when we withdraw from vices and weep for our former sins; but if, persisting in our crimes, we think that we can buy the ears of God with vows and sacrifices, we greatly err, judging God to be unjust. For he who has once been destined for the sword and famine and pestilence cannot be rescued by any prayers. Hence the prophet too is told not to ask in vain for what he cannot obtain.

14:13.t: And I said: Ah, ah, ah, Lord God — or you who are, Lord God —, the prophets say to them: You shall not see the sword, and famine shall not be among you, but he will give you true peace in this place. And the Lord said to me: The prophets prophesy falsely in my name. I did not send them, and I did not command them, nor did I speak to them; a lying vision and deceitful divination and the seduction of their own heart they prophesy to you. Let the teachers hear this who promise prosperity to those who sin and persist in their vices, who say to the rich: 'You shall not see the sword of God's torments, and famine shall not be among you. For you will be filled with the words of God, and the Lord will give you most true peace in the place of the Church, or of Jerusalem'. But that, according to the Hebrew, he said three times: Ah, ah, ah, answers to what came before, where the Lord had threatened, saying: by the sword and by famine and by pestilence I will consume them.

14:14.t: Since, then, the prophets, nay rather the false prophets, promised false things, the Lord therefore spoke through Jeremiah: 'Do not listen to the words of the false prophets, who were not sent by me but came of their own will! Hence they are by no means to be called prophets but diviners, they who speak seduction to the people'. For it is much better to amend sins through fear of punishments than, through hope of prosperity, to fall under the divine sentence.

14:15.t: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name, whom I did not send, saying: Sword and famine shall not be in this land: by sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed. And the peoples to whom they have prophesied shall be cast out in the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword, and there shall be none to bury them, they and their wives, their sons and their daughters, and I will pour out upon them their own evil or their own evils. Let the false prophets beware, who by promising prosperity trip up the people of God, lest they themselves perish and the deceived people be destroyed by a like ruin, and they lie in the streets of Jerusalem and, trampling on the precepts of the Lord, perish by famine and sword, and there be none to bury them nor to cover their disgrace with the dust of repentance. For the prophets themselves and the people, and their wives, and sons and daughters, and their whole generation will be on the dunghill without any undertaker. […]

14:17.t: And you shall say this word to them: Let my eyes shed a tear — or let your eyes shed tears — through night and day, and let them not be silent — or let them not cease —, for the virgin daughter of my people has been crushed with a great crushing, with a most grievous blow, exceedingly. This passage is understood in two ways: either that God himself laments his people and his eyes do not cease to weep, or at any rate that he commands that the eyes of the peoples should flow with tears; and that what must be lamented is no light thing, since the virgin daughter of his people has been struck with the greatest crushing and an intolerable blow. Others think that these things are said in the person of the prophet.

14:18.t: If I go out into the fields, behold, those slain by the sword, and if I enter the city, behold, those wasted with famine — or the pain of famine —! The prophet also and the priest have gone off into a land which they did not know. A just cause for lamenting, that the virgin has been crushed, the daughter struck and the people destroyed. 'For if,' he says, 'I wish to go outside, I shall see the slain; if to enter the city, I shall behold those wasted and scarcely clinging to their bones through the necessity of famine'. And what wonder is it to say this of the common people and the ignoble crowd, when the prophets also and the priests, who prophesied prosperity to others and who ought to have opened the commandments of the law, themselves went into a land which they did not know and endured the evil of captivity? […]

14:19.t: Have you utterly cast off Judah, or has your soul abhorred Zion? Why then have you struck us, so that there is no healing? We waited for peace, and there is no good, and for a time of healing, and behold, turmoil! The prophet marvels that the Lord has so suddenly cast off Judah and Jerusalem, that is, the kingdom of the two tribes, in which were the religion of God and the ceremonies of the temple, and has struck them with so great a blow that no medicine can be applied. 'We waited', he says, 'for peace and for a time of healing, and there is no good at all, but, on the contrary, turmoil, so that where formerly there had been the worship of God and tranquility, there all things were filled with seditions and the roar of the enemy'. If ever, therefore, our Zion too and our Judah is cast off and the soul of God abhors it, let us by no means marvel, but rather let us say what follows:

14:20.t: We have acknowledged, O Lord, our impieties, the iniquity of our fathers, because we have sinned against you. 'Both we', he says, 'and our fathers, with the same madness, neglected the precepts of God, and the measure of our forefathers has been filled up in us, so that whatever had been lacking in them was completed by our heap'. Hence it is also said of Judas: Let the iniquity of his fathers return to remembrance in the sight of the Lord, and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out! Let it be over against the Lord always, and let the memory of them perish from the earth!

14:21.t: Do not give us over to reproach for your name's sake, nor bring upon us the dishonor of the throne of your glory! Remember, do not make void your covenant with us! Let us consider the throne of God's glory to be not only the temple of Judea, which has often been destroyed, but every saint, in whom, according to that which is written: You have dashed his throne to the ground, it is dashed down and destroyed when he has offended God by a multitude of sins; but nevertheless he who has perished by his own fault is upheld by the clemency of the Lord, which is exchanged for the severity of the sentence if the Lord makes void his pact, by which he has promised that we shall be saved.

14:22.t: Are there among the graven images of the nations any that rain, or can the heavens give showers? Are you not the Lord God, whom we have awaited? For you have made all these things. After many and varied discourses he returns to the title of the prophecy, in which it is written: the word of the Lord which came to Jeremiah concerning the words of the drought. So what he says is this: 'Since the images of demons cannot rain, nor can the heavens of themselves give their shower, therefore you, O Lord our God, whom we have always awaited, to whom we have turned our hopes and vows, you give your rain! For all things are yours, and whatever is good cannot be given without you, whose it is'. Let us say this also against the heretics, who cannot bestow the rain of doctrines, and who, though they promise that they are heavens and boast that it is written of them: The heavens declare the glory of God, nevertheless cannot give the showers of doctrine. […]

15:1.t: And the Lord said to me: if Moses and Samuel stand before me — or against me —, my soul is not toward this people. For we read that these men withstood the wrath of the Lord on behalf of the people and turned aside a sentence that was already impending. 'Even if', he says, 'they stand either in my sight or against me' — to one of whom God said: Let me alone, and I will strike this people —, 'yet I will not hear, because the crimes of the offending people are complete'.
Cast — or send — them out from my face, and let them go forth! Sinners withdraw from God not in place but in will, although we read that both Adam and Cain were cast out from the face of God.

Hence the Truth says: "When you stand to pray, forgive if you have anything in your hearts." We show the virtue of forgiveness more clearly if we bring forward one testimony from the Old Testament. Certainly when Judea had offended the justice of its Creator through its demanding sins, the Lord, forbidding His prophet from prayer, says: "Do not take up praise and prayer for them. If Moses and Samuel stood before me, my soul would not be toward this people." What is it that, with so many fathers passed over and left aside, Moses and Samuel alone are brought forward, whose wondrous power of obtaining is shown, while even they are said to be unable to intercede? As if the Lord were saying openly: I do not even hear those whom I by no means despise on account of the great merit of their petition. What then is it that Moses and Samuel are preferred to the other fathers in petition, except that these two alone in the entire sequence of the Old Testament are read to have prayed even for their enemies? […]

15:2.t: And if they say to you: where shall we go forth?, you will say to them: thus says the Lord: those for death, to death, and those for the sword, to the sword, and those for famine, to famine, and those for captivity, to captivity! And I will visit upon them four kinds, says the Lord: the sword for slaying, and dogs for tearing, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth for devouring and scattering. The prophecy of Ezekiel also shows four plagues to which the people of the Jews was handed over: the sword, pestilence from famine, beasts, captivity. Among the beasts, moreover, understand the dogs and the birds as well, to which they were handed over for their bodies to be torn and devoured and scattered. For it could not happen that, once the Creator was neglected, the whole creation should not rise up against sinners.

15:4.t: And I will give them over to ferment — or commotion and distresses — to all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for all that he did in Jerusalem. We read in the book of Chronicles that Manasseh, after his captivity and repentance, returned to Jerusalem and reigned; but just as the merits of the saints descend to their posterity, as in the case of David and the rest, so the outrages of sinners reach their posterity, if their children and grandchildren have done similar things. But what he says: 'I will give them over to ferment or commotion and distresses of the whole earth', was both fulfilled in part under the Babylonians and is now being fulfilled in full, since the impious people imitated a most wicked king, one who filled Jerusalem from gate to gate with the blood of the righteous. From this we learn that peoples are very often destroyed by the crime of kings and princes and of those set over them.

15:5.t: We wish to understand the words spoken to Jerusalem with much menace, which run thus: "Who will spare you, O Jerusalem? Or who will be sorrowful for you? Or who will turn aside to ask after your peace? You have turned away from me, says the Lord. You shall go backward, and I will stretch out my hand against you and destroy you, and I will no longer let you go. And I will scatter them in a dispersion." Then: "I have been made childless." Perplexity has seized me. I take as an illustration a man who has been declared an enemy of the one who reigns upon the earth, because for such a person it is not permitted even to impart mercy, lest anyone seem to give offense to the king who has condemned him. And it is not permitted even to show mercy to such a one; some go still further and do not even show sorrow over him, lest by showing sorrow they seem to be displeased with the sentence passed by the king. […]

For who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? or who will grieve for you? or who will go to ask for your peace? For when God has been offended no one can intercede for the outrages of sinners, because a creature cannot be as merciful as the Maker, nor can a stranger spare outsiders as the Lord spares his own.

15:6.t: And to each interpretation of Jerusalem what follows will also fit: "You have turned away from me, says the Lord. You shall go backward." That you have turned away from the Son of God, and because of having turned away from the Son of God you have turned away from God — what need is there even to say it? And since Jerusalem in Judea turned away from Christ — from which we must understand all the Jews — for this reason "you shall go backward." For there was a time when she did not go backward, but forward; but now she goes backward, and "they turned in their hearts to Egypt," clearly so that they might go backward. But concerning what "you shall go backward" means, or what it is to reach forward to the things that are ahead, we shall present it thus. The righteous man "reaches forward to the things that are ahead, forgetting the things that are behind." Clearly the one disposed contrary to the righteous man remembers the things behind and does not reach forward to the things that are ahead. […]

You have forsaken me, says the Lord; you have gone backward. The reason is given why no one should have pity on Jerusalem, or grieve for her, or entreat for her peace: that, although according to the Apostle she ought, forgetting what lies behind, to have stretched forward to what lies before, she on the contrary turned back and longed for the meats of Egypt.

And I will stretch out my hand over you and kill you; I have labored, being entreated — or entreating —, for which the Seventy translated: I will by no means forgive them any longer. An outstretched hand is the sign of one who strikes; the killing of sinners signifies wrath brought to completion. But what he added: I have labored, being entreated or entreating, has a twofold sense: that God has already grown faint from often forgiving them, and that he is weary from always calling them to salvation.

15:7.t: And I will scatter them with a winnowing fan in the gates of the land — or of my people —; I have killed and destroyed my people, and yet they have not turned back from their ways. 'What does it profit that I am entreated so often, when they do not turn back from their most wicked ways nor do repentance? For I scattered them as with a winnowing fan, to purge my threshing floor, and I scattered them in the gates of the land, so that in a manner they might tread the thresholds of hell, and I have killed and destroyed my people, so that, compelled by the necessity of evils, they might avoid the evils that were impending'.

There are also other sorts of vengeance, with which some who have overpassed the bounds of wickedness are smitten in this life, as we read that Dathan and Abiram or Korah were punished, or above all, those of whom the Apostle speaks: "Wherefore God gave them up to vile passions and a reprobate mind:" and this must be counted worse than all other punishments. For of these the Psalmist says: "They are not in the labours of men; neither shall they be scourged like other men." For theyare not worthy of being healed by the visitation of the Lord which gives life, and by plagues in this world, as "in despair they have given themselves over to lasciviousness, unto the working of all error unto uncleanness," and as by hardening their hearts, and by growing accustomed and used to sin they have got beyond cleansing in this brief life and punishment in the present world: men, who are thus reproved by the holy word of the prophet: "I destroyed some of you, as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were as a firebrand plucked […]

15:8.t: Her widows have been multiplied to me above the sand of the sea; I have brought upon them, upon the mother of the young man, a destroyer at noon; I have sent terror suddenly upon the cities. God desires to save sinners by various remedies, so that those who had despised him when he coaxed them may fear him when he threatens. The widows were multiplied above the sand of the sea when their husbands had been slain; the mothers, having lost their children, felt the destroyer not at night and through ambushes, but in broad daylight, to show the open force of a stronger adversary. 'I have sent', he says, 'upon the cities' — no doubt those of Judah and of the sinful people — 'terror suddenly, so that, the more sudden the evil was, the more difficult escape would be'.

15:9.t: "In that day, saith the Lord, the sun shall go down at noon, and there shall be darkness over the earth in the clear day; and I will turn your feast days into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation," plainly announced that obscuration of the sun which at the time of His crucifixion took place from the sixth hour onwards, and that after this event, those days which were their festivals according to the law, and their songs, should be changed into grief and lamentation when they were handed over to the Gentiles. Jeremiah, too, makes this point still clearer, when he thus speaks concerning Jerusalem: "She that hath born [seven] languisheth; her soul hath become weary; her sun hath gone down while it was yet noon; she hath been confounded, and suffered reproach: the remainder of them will I give to the sword in the sight of their enemies." […]

The Scriptures prophesied that at noon in Christ's passion there should be darkness. In Amos it says, "And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, the sun shall set at noon, and the day of light shall be darkened. I will turn your feast days into grief and all your songs into lamentation." Also in Jeremiah: "She is frightened that has borne children, and her soul has grown weary. Her sun has gone down while as yet it was noon. She has been confounded and accursed. I will give the rest of them to the sword in the sight of their enemies." Also in the Gospel: "Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the earth even to the ninth hour."
15:9.s: Treatise XII. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews 2:23

15:9.t: She is weakened — or has cast away or has been made empty —, who bore seven — or very many —, her soul has fainted; the sun has set for her while it was still day — or midday —; she is confounded and has blushed. And her remnant I will give to the sword in the sight of their enemies, says the Lord. We have often said that the Hebrew word 'saba' means either 'seven' or 'oath' or 'very many'. Hence the translation also differs, Aquila, the Seventy and Theodotion translating 'seven', Symmachus 'very many'. She, then, who was rich in children was suddenly made childless, and perished in broad daylight, and was confounded in her own desolation. 'But the remnant of the people', he says, 'I will hand over to the sword, so that no one may escape death and the wrath of God'. Others refer it to the synagogue, which was weakened so that the multitude of the Church might grow, according to what is written: The barren has borne seven — or very many — and she who had many children has been weakened. […]

15:10.t:
Physicians of bodies, being present with the sick and always devoting themselves to the care of the ailing according to the intent of the medical art, look upon dreadful things and touch loathsome ones; from the misfortunes of others they reap their own griefs, and their life is always in the midst of hardship. For they are never with the healthy, but always with the wounded, with those who have festering sores, with those full of pus, of fevers, of manifold diseases. And if anyone wishes to make ready the practice of medicine, he will not be indignant nor neglect the intent of the art which he has taken up, whenever he is among such people as we have described.

I have spoken this preface because the prophets too are, as it were, physicians of souls, and they always spend their time where those who need healing are; for "it is not the healthy who have need of a physician, but those who are ill." […]

Those who call the prophets blessed, and who by calling them blessed pray to have their portion with the prophets, gather from the prophetic words the choicest features of their prophecy. Seeking, then, they might be persuaded—if they should live according to these things (even if it should turn out hard for them in this life to imitate the prophetic life)—that they will attain rest and blessedness together with the prophets. Now it is possible from many sources to gather the choice qualities of the prophets: their freedom, their vigor, their wakefulness, their alertness—that they were not anxious when they found themselves in dire circumstances, because of their freedom, their only concern being to reprove, to convert, as prophets do, by speaking the word of God with boldness, rebuking the sinners, even though those being reproved seemed to have great power. But even if it is possible to do this from every source, let us look also at the passages read today. […]

Jeremiah also bewails his birth in these words: "Woe is me, my mother! Why have you borne me, a man of contention in all the earth? I have not benefited others, nor has anyone benefited me. My strength has failed." If, then, holy people shrink from life whose life, though profitable to us, they themselves consider unprofitable, what ought we to do who are not able to profit others and who feel that our lives, like money borrowed at interest, grow more heavily weighted every day with an increasing mass of sins? "I die daily," says the apostle. Better certainly is this saying than those who say that meditation on death is true philosophy, for while they praise the study, he exercises the practice of death.

Woe is me, my mother, why did you bear me a man of strife — or of judgment —, a man of discord — or who am to be judged — in the whole earth? This can be understood synekdochikōs [by synecdoche] of Jeremiah, since he was judged not in the whole world but in the land of Judea. But it truly befits the Lord, the Savior, who says in the Gospel: For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind, of whom it is written: Behold, this one is set for the fall and the rising of many in Israel, and for a sign that will be contradicted. For which of the philosophers, which of the Gentiles, which of the heretics does not judge Christ, laying down laws for him concerning his birth and passion and resurrection and substance? […]

I have not lent at interest, nor has anyone lent at interest to me; all curse me, for which LXX: I have not profited, nor has anyone profited me, Theodotion: I have not owed, nor has anyone owed me. The sense of all of these, in the person of Christ, is this: 'No one has offered himself who would worthily receive my money, nor has anyone lent at interest to me by making me his debtor in cherishing the saints and the poor. Or I have not profited, nor has anyone profited me; for no one has been willing to receive as much as I desired to bestow. Nor has anyone profited me; for the salvation of the creature is the gain of the Creator. Or certainly I have not owed, nor has anyone owed me; no one has given me as much as I desired to receive, nor has he made me his debtor in anything'. And what he adds: nor has anyone owed me, has this sense: 'For how could he owe me interest, who did not deign to accept a loan?' All, he says, curse me; […]

In place of what we translated according to the Hebrew: all curse me, up to the place where it is written: in the time of tribulation against the enemy, I have found it written thus in the common edition: My strength has failed in those who curse me. So be it, Lord, with them being directed, if I did not stand by you in the time of their affliction and in the time of their tribulation for good against the enemy! And the sense is: 'My strength has failed in those who curse me; for they do not understand my power, which is made perfect in weakness, and the more they curse me, the more my strength fails in them'. And either the prophet or the Lord joins to this and says: So be it, Lord, with them being directed! That is: 'Let the curses which the enemies speak come upon me, and let them be directed into good, if in the time of their tribulation and distress, when the enemy was laying them waste and hastening to capture them, I did not stand in your sight and entreat you for them and say: Father, forgive them; […]

15:11.t: "So be it, Lord, when they set straight their way; did I not stand by you in the time of their evils?" What is "So be it, Lord"? Let the one who is able gather such a meaning for himself. [The "So be it"—] "Master, Lord, when they set straight their way"—may the strength that fails among those who curse come to be, when, having repented after speaking evil of me, they turn to the straight path and travel it. "So be it, Master, when they set straight their way; did I not stand by you?" Then he pleads his cause concerning those who speak evil of him, saying: "Did I not stand by you in the time of their evils?" He stood by the Father, ⟨being a propitiation for our sins,⟩ and interceded concerning them in that very time of our evils. For he did not stand by after the time of our evils, but "while we were yet sinners Christ died for us"—"Did I not stand by you in the time of their evils, in the time of their afflictions, for good against the enemy?" […]

The Lord says: if your remnant is not for good, if I did not meet you in the time of affliction and in the time of tribulation — and of distress — against the enemy. These words can also be taken in the person of Jeremiah, who was compelled to prophesy in a most evil time, with captivity already imminent, and to suffer hard things from an unbelieving people. To what he had said above: Woe is me, mother, why did you bear me a man who am to be judged and contended with by all the earth? and the rest, the Lord answers: 'Do not consider the present, but the future; for your remnant and your last things will be for good. Indeed even at present, when the enemies desired to crush you, I was at your side, and you were protected by my help'. This, moreover, can be referred as well to Jeremiah as, according to the dispensation of the flesh he assumed, to the Savior.

15:12.t: Upon these things [what] does God answer to the people that was accused by the prophet or by Christ, and he says these things to it: "Iron and a covering of bronze is your strength"—hard, unyielding, not to be hammered out. "Iron and a covering of bronze is your strength," that is, your strength is something cutting and dividing, a strength not existing for good.

Shall iron be leagued with iron from the north, and bronze? Symmachus: Shall iron harm iron from the north, and bronze? LXX and Theodotion: If iron will know, and a covering of bronze? The cause of the variety is clear; for the word 'iare', which is written in the present place, owing to the ambiguity of its pronunciation means both 'friendship' and 'malice'; and if, in place of the letter 'res', which is similar to the letter 'daleth', 'daleth' is read, it signifies 'knowledge and understanding'. What is said is to be understood thus: 'Do not grieve that the people is your enemy; for when you announce hard things, one who is hard cannot love you': either the Babylonians, who come from the north and are the hardest iron, will not be able to be joined in friendship with this people, which is harder and untamed after the likeness of bronze; or the hardest iron, that is, the people of Israel, is unworthy of the knowledge of God, since it has come to such malice that it is encased in a harder metal, bronze.

15:13.t:
"And I will give your treasures for plunder, as an exchange for all your sins." What "treasures" of the sinners does God give "for plunder," and give them "as an exchange for all their sins"? Is it perchance those treasured up for themselves on earth? For each of men treasures up: if he is base, upon earth; but if he is refined, in heaven, as we were taught from the Gospel. Or does he say to that people, that I am about to give your treasures for plunder because of your sins? What treasures of that people were given for plunder? Behold, one of the treasures is Jeremiah, another treasure is Isaiah, a treasure was Moses too. These treasures God took from that people, and through Christ—who said, "The kingdom of God shall be taken away from you and shall be given to a nation producing its fruits"—he gave to us.

"I will give," then, "because of your sins your treasures for plunder." And he gave the treasures of that people to us; […]

Your riches and your treasures I will give up for plunder for nothing — or without price — for all your sins and in all your borders. And I will bring your enemies — or I will make you serve your enemies — from a land which you do not know, because a fire has been kindled in my fury; it will burn upon you. 'All your substance', he says, 'I will hand over to your enemies without any price, on account of the sins which you have committed in all your borders. Therefore I will bring your enemies or I will make you serve in the land of Chaldea, because my fire, once kindled in my fury, will burn in you and cannot be extinguished; for you have furnished the material for your own burning, so that my fire may consume your wood, which is in you, and hay and stubble'. And so the cause of the burning is not in the Lord, but in those who supplied fuel to the fire.

15:14.t: "And I will make you a slave among all your enemies in the land which you did not know." That people has been enslaved among its enemies, and has come to be in the land which it did not know. "Because a fire has been kindled out of my wrath; it shall be burned upon you."

15:15.t: After these things and the words of the threats spoken to the people, the one who prayed above completes his prayer and joins to the aforesaid these words: "You know, Lord; remember me and visit me, and acquit me from those who persecute me, not unto long-suffering." And let the prophet say these things, persecuted by those he reproved, hated by those who cannot contain the truth; for he became an enemy to his hearers by speaking the truth to them. And let our Savior too say these same things, who was also persecuted by the people and says: "not unto long-suffering." What is the "not unto long-suffering"? You have always been long-suffering toward the people over their sins, but over the things dared against me do not be long-suffering. And truly God was not long-suffering. If you examine the times of the passion and of the fall of Jerusalem and of the razing of the city, and in what manner God abandoned that people, since they killed Christ, you will see that he no longer used long-suffering toward the people. […]

You know, Lord: remember me and visit me, and deliver me from those who persecute me! Do not take me up in your patience; know that I have borne reproach for you! Your words were found, and I ate them — or by those who reject your words; consume them — and your word became to me — or will be to me — a joy and the gladness of my heart, because your name has been called upon me, O Lord God of hosts! What we said: 'You know', is not found in the Seventy. Happy, moreover, is that conscience which bears reproach for God. Hence he says: 'Your words were found, which you were speaking by my mouth, and I ate them, that is: they were turned into food for me'; or, according to Symmachus: 'I received them, so that they were turned into gladness for me, though formerly they had been a reproach'. Hence the Babylonians too confess that what Jeremiah had foretold as future has been fulfilled. […]

15:16.t: "And your word shall be to me for gladness." It is not now, but "shall be"; for since at present your word is to me for imprisonments, for trials, for troubles, for defamations, for pains — yet the end of these shall be gladness. "And your word shall be to me for gladness and joy of my heart, because your name has been called upon me, Lord Almighty." And if Christ says it, the name of the Father has been called upon him.

15:17.t: "I did not sit in the assembly of them when they made sport." If ever the prophet saw the assembly not of those in earnest but of those making sport, he fled from being gathered together rather than hastened toward the gathering of those making sport. You must, then, understand the difference between an assembly of those making sport and of those in earnest. This assembly is earnest and does all things with earnestness and things worthy of earnestness, and according to the saying: the word is earnestness, the life is earnestness, and altogether the assembly is not of those making sport, but of those in earnest. But whenever the assembly, forsaking the earnestness about necessary things, gives its leisure to the playthings of this age and to the playthings that come from wickedness, it becomes an assembly of those making sport. This one, then, says: "I did not sit in the assembly of them when they made sport, but I was in awe before the presence of your hand." […]

Jeremiah was in captivity; but there were also many multitudes. And what does he say? I sat alone, because I was filled with bitterness. How were you alone in the city? But therefore alone, because I had no companion of my purpose.

I did not sit in the council of those who make merry, and I gloried; — or I was afraid — before the face of your hand I sat alone, because you filled me with bitterness. Why has my pain become perpetual — or why are those who sadden me strengthened — and my desperate wound refused to be healed — or my wound is strong; whence shall I be healed —? It has become to me as a lie of faithless waters or as lying water that has no faithfulness. The Hebrews think that these words are spoken in the person of Jerusalem: that she sat alone and was filled with bitterness, and her pain became perpetual, and that, as waters pass away, so the words of the prophets, by which they promised themselves prosperity, passed away falsely. […]

15:18.t:
"Why do those who hate me prevail?" He had many troubles; he suffered from those who did not wish to hear the truth, and those men were more powerful than he here in this age, since the kingdom of God is not from this age, but from the better regions, as the Savior says: "If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would have striven, that I should not be delivered to the Jews." Those, then, who grieved the prophet prevailed over him in this world. For that they do prevail, look at the martyrs. The judge sits giving judgment and living luxuriously in the tribunal; the Christian, in whom Christ is being judged, was filled with bitterness and is overpowered by the unjust man and is condemned.

"My wound is firm, whence shall I be healed?" Those who prevail over me strike me, and my wound is firm. […]

How then can one who is baptized among them seem to have obtained remission of sins and the grace of the divine mercy by his faith, when he has not the truth of the faith itself? For if, as some suppose, one could receive anything abroad out of the church according to his faith, certainly he has received what he believed. If he believes what is false, he could not receive what is true. Rather, he has received things adulterous and profane, according to what he believed. Jeremiah, the prophet, censures in detail this subject of profane and adulterous baptism, saying, "Why do those who grieve me prevail? My wound is incurable. When shall I be healed? When this is done, it is become for me as treacherous water not having faith." The Holy Spirit makes mention through the prophet of treacherous water also not having faith. What is this treacherous and faithless water? Assuredly it is that which asserts falsely the image of baptism and frustrates the grace of faith by its shadowy simulation.

Now the so-called gods of the Greeks, unworthy of the name, are faithful neither in their essence nor in their promises, because they are not everywhere. The local deities amount to nothing over the course of time and undergo a natural extinction. For these reasons, the Word cries out against them, that "faith is not strong in them," that they are "waters that fail" and "there is no faith in them." But the God of all, who is indeed truly faithful, who is ever the same, says, "See now that I, even I am he," and "I change not." Therefore, his Son is "faithful," being ever the same and unchanging, deceiving neither in his essence nor in his promise, as is written by the apostle to the Thessalonians: "Faithful is he who calls you, who also will do it." For in doing what he promises, he is faithful to his words.

15:19.t: "Therefore thus says the Lord: If you return, then I will restore you." These things again are said to each one whom God shall exhort to return to him. And a mystery seems to me to be indicated here in the "I will restore you." No one is restored to a place in which he has in no way ever been, but the restoration is to what is one's own. For instance, if a limb of mine becomes dislocated, the physician tries to make a restoration of what is dislocated. When someone comes to be outside his homeland, whether justly or unjustly, and then recovers the ability to be again in the homeland according to the laws, he has been restored to his own homeland. Understand the same for me also in the case of a soldier who has been cast out from his own ranks and is restored. He says, then, here to us who have turned away, that if we return, he will restore us. […]

Let us catch them then by our mode of life; and by these souls let us build up the Church, and of these let us amass our wealth. There is nothing to weigh against a soul, not even the whole world. So that although thou give countless treasure unto the poor, thou wilt do no such work as he who converteth one soul. "For he that taketh forth the precious from the vile shall be as my mouth:" so He speaks. A great good it is, I grant, to have pity on the poor; but it is nothing equal to the withdrawing them from error.

Words full of gentleness and meekness, even as also He Himself used to speak, saying to them that were insulting Him, "I have not a devil;" and again, "If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil." If thou also speak in this way; if thou speak for thy neighbor's amendment, thou wilt obtain a tongue like that tongue. And these things God Himself saith; "For he that bringeth out the precious from the vile, shall be as my mouth;" such are His words. When therefore thy tongue is as Christ's tongue, and thy mouth is become the mouth of the Father, and thou art a temple of the Holy Ghost, then what kind of honor could be equal to this?
15:19.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 78:2

15:19.t: Therefore thus says the Lord: if you turn, I will turn you, and you will stand before my face; and if you separate the precious from the vile, you will be as my mouth; they will turn to you, and you will not turn to them. And I will give you to this people for a wall of bronze, strong, and they will fight against you and will not prevail, because I am with you to save you and deliver you, says the Lord. And I will free you from the hand of the most wicked and redeem you from the hand of the strong or of the pestilent. It is clear that it was by no means Jerusalem but the prophet who said the preceding words. To him the Lord answers: 'If you turn the people from their sins, I too will turn you from tribulation into gladness, and you will stand before my face, as the angels stand in the sight of God, daily seeing his face, and if you separate the precious from the vile, you will be as my mouth. And do not think', he says, 'that there is no reward for a good work; […]

16:2.t: Elijah lived a virgin life; so also did Elisha and many of the sons of the prophets. To Jeremiah the command came: "You will not take a wife." He had been sanctified in his mother's womb, and now he was forbidden to take a wife because the captivity was near. The apostle gives the same counsel in different words: "I think, therefore, that this is good by reason of the present distress, namely, that it is good for a person to be as he is." What is this distress that does away with the joys of wedlock? The apostle tells us, in a later verse: "The time is short. It remains that those who have wives be as though they had none."

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Do not take a wife, and let there be no sons and daughters for you in this place! For thus says the Lord concerning the sons and daughters who are begotten in this place, and concerning their mothers who bore them, and concerning their fathers, of whose stock they were born in this land: They shall die by the deaths of sicknesses; they shall not be lamented and they shall not be buried; they shall be as dung upon the face of the earth, and they shall be consumed by the sword and by famine, and their corpses shall be food for the birds of heaven and for the beasts of the earth. If, at the time of the impending captivity, the prophet is forbidden to marry a wife, so that he may not have tribulation of the flesh and, on top of his own grief, be tormented also by the miseries of his wife and children, how much more does the Apostle command, because the time has been shortened and the consummation is at hand, that even those who have wives should be as though they had none! […]

16:3.t: But why the prophet is kept from marrying a wife, the reason is plain: because with the siege close at hand all were to perish by pestilence and sword and famine, and the number of the dying would be so great that the duty of burial would be overwhelmed, and the corpses would lie like dung to be torn by birds and beasts. And this too must be noted, that to waste away through sicknesses and long infirmity is the wrath of God. Hence Joram also, the son of Jehoshaphat, is consumed by infirmity, and the Apostle teaches that those who have violated holy things fall sick and waste away and die.

16:5.t: For thus says the Lord: Do not enter the house of feasting, nor go to lament, nor comfort them, for I have taken away my peace from this people, says the Lord, my mercy and compassions. And both great and small shall die in this land; they shall not be buried nor lamented, and they shall not cut themselves, nor shall baldness be made for them. And they shall not break bread among them for the mourner, to comfort him over the dead, and they shall not give them the drink of the cup to comfort them over their father and mother. And you shall not enter the house of feasting, to sit with them and eat and drink. The Apostle commands that with those who turn away from God not even food is to be taken; and further: do not even say hail to such! And the Savior forbids the apostles to greet anyone on the way; hence Elisha too forbids Gehazi to give greetings as he went to heal the boy. […]

16:9.t: For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will take away from this place, before your eyes and in your days, the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride. And when you have announced to this people all these words, and they have said to you: Why has the Lord spoken all this great evil against us?
