And theirs is the new covenant, not according to the old. Do not allow the covenant of the pre-Mosaic Saints to be called "the old covenant,"but that which was given to the Jews by the Law of Moses. For the text which says that the new will be quite unlike the old clearly implies which one was the old:

"I will make a new covenant, not according to the covenant I made with their fathers, in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt."

"Not according to the covenant of the Mosaic Law,"he says. For that was introduced to the Jews at the exodus from Egypt. It might have seemed that he was introducing a new covenant opposed to the religious ideals of the Abrahamic Saints, if he had not distinctly said:

"Not according to the covenant, which I made with their fathers, in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt." […]
31:31.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 1, Chapter 6

31:31.t:
This new song is called by Jeremiah, another Hebrew prophet, "a new covenant"where he says:

"31. Behold the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Juda: 32. not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt: for they abode not in my covenant, and I disregarded them, saith the Lord. 33. For this is my, covenant which I will make with the house of Israel, saith the Lord, I will put my laws in their minds, and on their hearts I will write (them), and I will be their God, and they shall be my people."

You see here that he distinguishes two covenants, the old and the new, and says that the new would not be like the old which was given to the fathers. […]
31:31.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 1, Chapter 4

31:31.t:
And we heard just now what the ordinances of the prophet were, which we must obey, their wisdom, perfection and heavenliness, which he thought fit to inscribe, not on tables of stone like Moses, nor yet with ink and parchment, but on the hearts of his pupils, purified and open to reason. On them he wrote the laws of the new covenant, and actually fulfilled the prophecy of Jeremiah.

"I will make a new covenant, not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers. For this is the covenant which I will make with the house of Israel, I will give my laws into their mind, and upon their heart I will write them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

THE one wrote on lifeless tables, the Other wrote the perfect commandments of the new covenant on living minds.
31:31.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 1, Chapters 7-8

31:31.t: IF THE LAW AND THE PROPHETS WERE UNTIL JOHN, HOW IS IT THAT THE SAVIOR SENDS THE LEPER TO THE PRIESTS TO HAVE OFFERINGS MADE FOR HIS CLEANSING (Matt. 8:4; Mark 1:44; Luke 5:14)? — This was done not because of the time, but for the condemnation of the Jews: so that when they did not understand that the summit of truth, belonging to a better time, had been established for the gain of their salvation, Truth might bend down instead to their accusation. For since they regarded the Savior as an enemy of the Law, because for the sake of mercy he wished to free them from the burden of the Law, just as had been foretold by the prophet Jeremiah, for he says among other things, “And I will give them a new covenant, not like the one I gave to their fathers” (Jer. 31:31–32), then the Savior, so that he might not appear, as they thought, to be an enemy when preaching new things, sent the man who had been cleansed from leprosy to the priests to offer gifts for his cleansing, as Moses had commanded (Lev. 14:2). […]
31:31.s: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 60: WHY THE SAVIOR SENT THE CLEANSED LEPER TO THE PRIESTS

31:31.t: See ye not how their reasoning comes round to the very contrary? how the God of the old covenant, whom they call cruel, will be found mild and meek: and He of the new, whom they acknowledged to be good, will be hard and grievous, according to their madness? Whereas we say, that there is but one and the same Legislator of either covenant, who dispensed all meetly, and adapted to the difference of the times the difference between the two systems of law. Therefore neither are the first commandments cruel, nor the second hard and grievous, but all of one and the same providential care. For that He Himself gave the old covenant also, hear the affirmation of the prophet, or rather (so we must speak), of Him who is both the one and the other: "I will make a covenant with you, not according to the covenant which I made with your fathers."
31:31.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 16:8

31:31.t: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will strike — or I will dispose — for the house of Israel and the house of Judah a new covenant — or testament — not according to the covenant — or testament — which I made with your fathers on the day when I took their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, a covenant — or testament — which they made void; and I ruled over them — or I neglected them —, says the Lord. And this will be the covenant — or testament — which I will strike with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law in their inward parts — or in the mind — and in their heart I will write it, and I will be to them for God and they shall be to me for a people. And they shall no longer teach, each one his neighbor and each one his brother, saying: know the Lord, for all shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest, says the Lord, for I will be propitious to their iniquity and of their sin I will be mindful no more. […]

From this it is clear that, according to the understanding of this perikopēs [passage], the foregoing is to be understood of the first coming of the Savior, when both peoples, Israel and Judah, were joined to each other. But if it raises a scruple for anyone why he said: I will dispose for the house of Israel and the house of Judah a new covenant — or testament — not according to the covenant which I made with your fathers, let him understand that the first Church of Christ was from the Jews, and that the Lord Savior came to them and said: I have not come except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and that the apostles confirmed this very thing: it was necessary that the word of God be spoken first to you; but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the nations. For it was not right to give the children's bread to dogs; […]

What say we to this? One nowhere, or hardly anywhere, except in this passage of the prophet, finds in the Old Testament Scriptures any mention so made of the New Testament as to indicate it by its very name. It is no doubt often referred to and foretold as about to be given, but not so plainly as to have its very name mentioned. Consider then carefully, what difference God has testified as existing between the two testaments - the old covenant and the new.
31:31.s: ON THE SPIRIT AND THE LETTER 33

31:31.t: It is then on account of the offence of the old man, which was by no means healed by the letter which commanded and threatened, that it is called the old covenant; whereas the other is called the new covenant, because of the newness of the spirit, which heals the new man of the fault of the old. Then consider what follows, and see in how clear a light the fact is placed, that men who bare faith are unwilling to trust in themselves: "Because," says he, "this is the covenant which I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the Lord, I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts."
31:31.s: ON THE SPIRIT AND THE LETTER 35

31:31.t: Yet a new covenant God promiseth us, now that "the first hath waxed old and is near to vanish away," according to the words of the divine Paul. Yea, He even says by one of tho holy prophets, "Behold the days come, saith the Lord, when I will perfect with the house of Israel, and with tho house of Judah, a new covenant: not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers in tho day when I took hold of their hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt." If therefore the new covenant is the second, and different from the first, there is every necessity for those who wish to live according to it, to abandon the old laws, and conform to those which will guide them into the newness of the gospel polity.
31:31.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

31:31.t: For that the institutions of Moses were intended to come to an end, and a new law and a new covenant to be given by Christ, any one may easily see, inasmuch as He says plainly; "Behold the days come, says the Lord, that I will appoint a new covenant for the house of Israel, and for the house of Judah; not according to the covenant that I appointed for their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide in My covenant, and I despised them, says the Lord." He promises therefore a new covenant: and as the very wise Paul writes, "In that He said, a new, He has made the former one old: but that which is made old, and growing old, is ready for destruction." Inasmuch therefore as the former (covenant) was made old, it was necessary that that which is new should enter in its place: and this was done not by one of the holy prophets, but by Him rather Who is the Lord of the prophets.
31:31.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

31:31.t:
By what law? of works? Nay, but by the law of faith. He calls faith here a law, not from inconsideration, but as recollecting the prophecy of Jeremiah (xxxi. 31, 32,) "For in those days, saith the Lord, and at that time, I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers."

If then the Mosaic law is thus styled a covenant, and the new covenant again bears also the same name, and faith in Christ be the law it enacts, in strict accordance with the phraseology of the prophet does the holy apostle here apply the name of the law to faith.

And therefore that the Lord might use outward healings as an introduction to inward remedies, and after healing bodies might work cures in the soul, He separated Himself from the surrounding crowd, ascended into the retirement of a neighbouring mountain, and called His apostles to Him there, that from the height of that mystic seat He might instruct them in the loftier doctrines, signifying from the very nature of the place and act that He it was who had once honoured Moses by speaking to him: then indeed with a more terrifying justice, but now with a holier mercifulness, that what had been promised might be fulfilled when the Prophet Jeremiah says: “behold the days come when I will complete a new covenant for the house of Israel and for the house of Judah. After those days, saith the Lord, I will put My laws in their minds, and in their heart will I write them.” […]

The same prophet again says: Lo! the days are coming, saith the Lord, and I shall make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. etc. This passage is cited by the Apostle in the Epistle to the Romans.

31:32.t: The number seven is passed away, the octave is arrived. Yesterday is gone, to-day is come, that promised day wherein we are admonished to hear and follow the word of God. That day of the Old Testament is passed away, that new day is come, wherein the New Testament is perfected, whereof it is said, "Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah; not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt." He adds too the reason why the Testament was changed, "Because they continued not in My covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord." The priests of the Law, the tribunals of the Law have passed away; let us draw nigh to our new High Priest, to the throne of grace, to the guest of our souls, to the Priest, Who is not made after the law of the carnal commandment, but elected after the power of an endless life. […]

There was a law, and there is a law. ("For the law of the Spirit of life hath made me free.") There was a service, and there is a service. ("To whom pertaineth the service"; and again: "Serving God in the Spirit.") There was a covenant, and there is a covenant. ("I will make with you a new covenant, not according to the covenant which I made with your fathers.") There was a sanctification, and there is a sanctification: there was a baptism, and there is a Baptism: there was a sacrifice, and there is a Sacrifice: there was a temple, and there is a temple: there was a circumcision, and there is a circumcision; and so too there was a "grace," and there is a "grace." But the words in the first case are used as types, in the second as realities, preserving a sameness of sound, though not of sense. So in patterns and figures, the shape of a man scratched with white lines upon a black ground is called a man as well as that which has received the correct coloring; […]
31:32.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 14

31:33.t: But now in the Gospel, after the cross, the resurrection and the ascension, he promises that he gives a covenant not on tablets of stone, but on fleshly tablets of the heart, and that, when the testament of the Lord has been written in the mind of believers, he himself is to them for God and they are to him for a people, so that they do not at all seek Jewish teachers and the traditions and commandments of men, but are taught by the Holy Spirit, if only they deserve to hear: you are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you. The Spirit, however, breathes where he wills, and has diverse graces, and the knowledge of the one God is the possession of all the virtues. 'And this', he says, 'will come about because I will be propitious to their iniquity and their sin I will remember no more.'

Accordingly, in our prophet likewise, whose testimony we are dealing with, this is added, that in God is the reward, in Him the end, in Him the perfection of happiness, in Him the sum of the blessed and eternal life. For after saying, "I will be their God, and they shall be my people," he at once adds, "And they shall no more teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me, from the least even unto the greatest of them."
31:33.s: ON THE SPIRIT AND THE LETTER 39

31:33.t: Here, God is Jerusalem's reward. Its highest—its entire—good is to possess him and to be possessed by him.

You should not write the creed out in any way, but, so as to hold the exact words of the creed, learn it by listening. Not even when you have learned it should you write it down, but, rather, always hold it and cherish it in your memory. For whatever you will hear in the creed is contained in the inspired books of the Holy Scriptures. The fact that it is not permitted to write down what has been thus collected and reduced to a definite form comes about in memory of the promise of God in which, predicting a New Testament, he said in the words of the prophet: "This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord, by setting my law in their minds, I will write it also in their hearts."

God proposes the most direct norms. Hence, the Apostle and Jeremiah say: "I will put my laws into their mind, and upon their hearts I will write them." For He inscribed them first in human nature, then in industry or progress, third in grace, and fourth in glory. In every state, He puts forth His rules: wherefore by necessity He must possess them within Himself.

31:34.t: He hath changed sunset into sunrise, and through the cross brought death to life; and having wrenched man from destruction, He hath raised him to the skies, transplanting mortality into immortality, and translating earth to heaven-He, the husbandman of God, "Pointing out the favourable signs and rousing the nations to good works, putting them in mind of the true sustenance;" having bestowed on us the truly great, divine, and inalienable inheritance of the Father, deifying man by heavenly teaching, putting His laws into our minds, and writing them on our hearts. What laws does He inscribe? "That all shall know God, from small to great;" and, "I will be merciful to them," says God, "and will not remember their sins." Let us receive the laws of life, let us comply with God's expostulations; let us become acquainted with Him, that He may be gracious.

Let me beg you to consider then this simple and single-hearted man, and take notice of him in the affairs of life, and you will see him a pattern of the utmost scrupulousness, such that if he would have shown it in spiritual matters he would not have been overlooked: for the facts of the truth are clearer than the sun. And wherever a man may go, he might easily lay hold of his own salvation, if he were minded, that is, to be heedful, and not to look on this as a by-work. For were the doings shut up into Palestine, or in a little corner of the world? Hast thou not heard the prophet say, "All shall know Me from the least even to the greatest?" Do not you see the things themselves uttering the truth? How then are these to be excused, seeing as they do the doctrine of the truth spread far and wide, and not troubling themselves?

In Jeremiah, we read concerning the future kingdom …, "They shall all know me, from the least to the greatest of them." The context of this passage clearly shows that the prophet is describing the future kingdom. But how can there possibly be in it a least or greatest, if all are to be equal? The secret is disclosed in the Gospel: "Whoever shall do and teach, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever shall teach and not do shall be least."

If we are asked why we do not worship God as the Hebrew fathers of the Old Testament worshipped Him, we reply that God has taught us differently by the New Testament fathers, and yet in no opposition to the Old Testament, but as that Testament itself predicted. For it is thus foretold by the prophet: "Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah; not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt." Thus it was foretold that that covenant would not continue, but that there would be a new one. And to the objection that we do not belong to the house of Israel or to the house of Judah, we answer according to the teaching of the apostle, who calls Christ the seed of Abraham, and says to us, as belonging to Christ's body, "Therefore ye are Abraham's seed."

You do not say, "Let man be made," but, "Let us make man." Nor do you say, "after his kind," but after "our image" and "likeness." Because, being renewed in his mind and beholding and apprehending your truth, a person does not need another person as his director so that he may imitate his own kind. By your direction he proves what your good, acceptable and perfect will is. You teach him—now that he has been made capable—to perceive the Trinity of the Unity and the Unity of the Trinity. Therefore this being said in the plural, "Let us make man," it is yet followed by the phrase in the singular, "and God made man." This is said in the plural, "after our likeness," followed by the phrase in the singular, "after the image of God." Thus humankind is renewed in the knowledge of God, after the image of him who created them. Being made spiritual, he judges all things—all things that are to be judged—"yet he himself is judged by no mortal."

The teachers of the Word come and go, and others follow in the succession of those who pass away. But the sacred Scripture remains for all time without ever being abolished, until the time when the Lord shall appear at the end of the world. Then we shall have no further need for the Scriptures or for those who interpret them, since there will be a long-awaited fulfillment of that promise of the Lord that says, "And they shall not teach their neighbor and brother saying, 'Know the Lord,' for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest."

31:35.t: Thus says the Lord, who gives the sun for the light of the day, the order of the moon and of the stars for the light of the night, who troubles the sea and its waves sound; the Lord of hosts is his name. If these laws — or these statutes — cease before me, says the Lord, then the seed of Israel too shall fail, so as not to be before me all the days. And at the beginning of Genesis we read that the sun was set in the heaven for the light of the day, and the moon too and the stars for the light of the night, and in the psalm: day to day utters the word and night to night shows knowledge, in that day and night succeed one another in turn. […]

31:37.t: Thus says the Lord: if the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth beneath searched out, I too will cast off the whole seed of Israel for all that they have done, says the Lord. LXX: thus says the Lord: if the heaven is raised higher and if the floor of the earth is lowered beneath, I too will not reject the race of Israel, says the Lord, for all that they have done. In this place the Hebrew differs much from the common edition. Let us speak first according to the Hebrew: 'if the heavens above can be measured and their height known, or the foundations of the earth searched out and their extremities comprehended by reason, I too', he says, 'will cast off the whole seed of Israel for all that they have done, says the Lord. But as that is impossible, that we should know the summits of the heavens and the foundations of the earth, so this too will be impossible, that I should cast off the whole seed of Israel. […]

31:38.t: Calling, therefore, upon the Lord Savior, who has the key of David, who opens, and no one shuts, and who shuts, and no one opens, who also opened the sealed book of Isaiah and of all the prophets, and whom the twenty-four elders holding harps adored, because he alone could unlock the divine mysteries, let us approach the building of the city to which the prophetic word is directed: glorious things are spoken of you, city of God, and: the rush of the river gladdens the city of God. The Church, then, is built from the tower 'of obedience' or 'of grace' and 'of the gifts of God' — for this is what Ananehel means — to the gate of the corner; which, though it seems to have a lofty beginning, yet as long as we abide in this flesh we cannot possess the straight line of truth, but we stand in the corner and in broken lines; […]

Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and the city shall be built for the Lord from the tower of Hananel to the gate of the corner. And the rule — or, according to Symmachus, the line — of its measure shall go out further, over against it, upon the hill Gareb, and it shall go round Goah — or, according to the LXX, of chosen stones — and all the valley of ruins — for which Theodotion put the Hebrew word itself, Phagarim — and the ashes and all Asaremoth — which we better read Asademoth, for which Aquila translated suburbs — to the brook Kidron and to the corner of the eastern gate of the horses, the holy place of the Lord; it shall not be plucked up and shall not be pulled down for ever. […]

31:40.t: And all, he says, the valley Phagarim — which means of ruins — and the ashes — 'it shall go round' is understood —, so that, although we seem to ourselves to be on hills, we may yet always fear ruins and consider ashes and, repenting, say with David: for I have eaten ashes like bread and mingled my drink with weeping. Whence also it is said to those who lie fallen: does not he who falls rise again?, says the Lord. And the whole, he says, Sademoth, which we render as the region of death, dividing one name into two words: 'sade', which is called 'region', and 'moth', which means 'of death', for which Aquila rendered 'suburbs' or 'fields' and 'countryside'. But the 'region' 'of death' is the region of sinners, and the 'suburbs' the region of pleasures, which goes on to the brook Kidron — where the Lord was betrayed —, which means 'darkness'. See how many places the Church has, and that that apostolic saying: 'that it be without spot and wrinkle', is reserved for the future and for the heavenly places. […]

32:1.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah; that is the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar. Then the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the house of the king of Judah. For Zedekiah, king of Judah, had shut him up, saying: Why do you prophesy, saying: Thus says the Lord? Not only the words but also the deeds of the prophets are an example to us for virtue. Jeremiah could have announced prosperity and enjoyed the friendship of King Zedekiah, but he preferred to obey God rather than men, and him who can kill both soul and body in Gehenna rather than him who could have power only over the body. And this must be considered: it was the tenth year of Zedekiah's reign, Jerusalem was already besieged and consumed by sword, famine and pestilence, captivity was near, and yet Zedekiah persists in his opinion; […]

32:3.t: Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it. And Zedekiah, king of Judah, shall not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and his mouth shall speak with his mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes. And he shall lead Zedekiah into Babylon, and there he shall be until I visit him, says the Lord. But if you fight against the Chaldeans, you shall have nothing prosperous. This was the cause of the king's anger: that he preferred truth to a lie, and said that both the city of Jerusalem and King Zedekiah were to be taken; and, what is more grievous, that he would see the face of the Babylonian king and, humbled and captive, would speak with the madness of a most violent king. For it is a heavier terror to see the one you fear, and to undergo the rebuke of words before the torment of punishments.

32:5.t: And into Babylon, he says, he shall lead Zedekiah, and there he shall be, for which the Seventy translated: and he shall enter Babylon; of which the one signifies being dragged unwilling, the other going of one's own will. And there, he says, he shall be: he puts an ambiguous word, so as not to seem to prophesy tortures and miseries. And what follows: until I visit him, says the Lord. And if you fight against the Chaldeans, you shall have nothing prosperous, is not in the Seventy. And he prudently tempered the sentence, which can be referred to a good and to a bad sense; for 'visitation', as I have often said, signifies both 'consolation' and 'punishment'.

32:6.t: And Jeremiah said: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Behold, Hanamel, the son of Shallum — or Salom —, your cousin — which in Hebrew is called 'dodach' —, is coming to you, saying: Buy for yourself my field, which is in Anathoth; for the purchase belongs to you by kinship. That the word of God had come secretly to Jeremiah no one could know unless he himself, to whom it had come, disclosed it. And it is foretold to him that Hanamel, his cousin, will come to him and offer him the possession of the field that had been his; and that the place itself is in Anathoth, among the suburban lands which were given by the law to the priests throughout the several tribes and cities; nor was it lawful for a possession to pass from tribe to tribe, nor from one family to another family — whence also the daughters of Zelophehad receive their lot among their brothers — and especially the suburban lands of the priests could be sold to no one else until the year of release, except to him whom nearness of blood required. […]

And thus it is that Matthew here relates what took place between Pilate and the Lord.

First, however, he makes a digression with the purpose of telling the story of Judas' end, which is related only by him. His account is in these terms: "Then Judas, which had betrayed Him, when he saw that He was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, saying, I have sinned, in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? See thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in. Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day. […]
32:6.s: The Harmony of the Gospels, Book 3, Chapter 7

32:8.t: And Hanamel, the son of my uncle, came to me according to the word of the Lord, to the vestibule — or court — of the prison, and said to me: Possess — or buy — my field, which is in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, because the inheritance belongs to you and you are the kinsman, so that you may possess or buy. What the word of the Lord had announced to the prophet as future was at once fulfilled in deed. 'There came', he says, 'to me Hanamel' — 'the grace of God' —, 'the son of my uncle' — that is, 'the son of peace' —; 'and he came into the vestibule of the prison and said to me the things which the Lord had foretold would be said by him'. And this priestly field, whose purchase and possession was being offered to Jeremiah, is in 'Anathoth', in the land of 'Beniamin', of which the first means 'obedience', the second 'son of the right hand'; and consequently he seeks the purchase of that place in which the 'obedience' and the 'power' of the Lord dwelt. […]

And I understood that it was the word of the Lord, and I bought the field from Hanamel, the son of my uncle, which is in Anathoth, and I weighed out the silver to him, seven and ten silver staters. And I wrote it in a book and sealed it and called witnesses and weighed the silver in the balance. And I took the book of possession, sealed, the stipulations and the ratifications and the seals on the outside. It was indeed hard, almost inconsistent and worthy of laughter, that he who was prophesying that Jerusalem was on the very point of being taken and that all were to be led captive or to perish by sword, famine and pestilence, should buy a field in Anathoth which he was not going to possess. 'But I understood', he says, 'that it was the word of the Lord, and that my purchase was to be fitted to the argument and prophecy of the Lord; […]

32:9.t: This is Jeremiah the tenth in order, who was also privileged to prophesy concerning the mystery respecting Christ, saying thus: And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was priced, whom certain of the sons of Israel did price, and they gave them for the potter's field as the Lord appointed me. The evangelist Matthew mentions this passage as having been fulfilled at the time of the passion.

32:10.t: In this number, then, the possession is bought by the prophet and priest, and it is written in a book and sealed, and witnesses are called and the silver is carefully weighed, so that all the rights of sale and purchase may be preserved and the possession may be certain, strengthened by stipulations and responses. Let them at least hear this who try to claim for themselves, by calling witnesses, wills that are false and sometimes not even wills at all!

32:12.t: And I gave the book of possession to Baruch, the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, in the eyes of Hanamel, my cousin, and in the eyes of the witnesses who were written in the book of purchase, in the eyes of all the Jews who were sitting in the court of the prison. Although the possession was at once to be abandoned — nay rather, it was being bought for posterity, and bought by one who had no sons, for he had not taken a wife —, yet, obedient to the command of the Lord, he performs everything duly and gives the sealed book of possession to Baruch, the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah. 'Baruch' in our language is called 'blessed'; he was the son of 'Neri', which means 'my lamp', as the prophet says: your word is a lamp to my feet and a burning light to my paths; and Neriah, Baruch's father, was in turn the son of 'Maasiae', that is, of 'making' and of 'the work of the Lord'. […]

32:13.t: And I commanded Baruch before them, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Take these books, this sealed book of purchase and this book which is open, and put them in an earthen vessel, that they may last many days. For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Houses and fields and vineyards shall yet be possessed in this land. With all those whom the preceding discourse has named present and looking on, Baruch, the minister and disciple, is commanded — not by the words of his teacher, but by the order of God who commands — to take the books, one sealed, the other open — a custom of purchases still kept to this day, so that what the seals hold shut up within, the open volume displays to those who wish to read it —, both of them in an earthen vessel, that they may last many days. […]

32:15.t: And all this is done so that those who saw it might understand that Jerusalem would again be inhabited and the fields possessed; and although they ought to have understood this by themselves without Jeremiah's word, yet they are admonished by the words of the Lord, and it is said to them: thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: houses and fields and vineyards shall yet be possessed in this land. This is what Jeremiah had said a little before: I understood that it was the word of the Lord; and for that reason he bought a field which he was not going to possess.

32:16.t: And I prayed to the Lord, after I had delivered the book of possession to Baruch, the son of Neriah, saying: Alas, alas, alas, Lord God — or you who are, Lord God —, behold, you made heaven and earth in your great strength and in your arm outstretched — or lofty —; not difficult for you — or impossible — shall be any word — or according to the Seventy nothing is hidden with you —, you who show mercy to thousands and repay the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their sons after them, most mighty, great, powerful — which in Hebrew is called 'gibbor' —, the Lord of hosts — or of powers — is your name! Great in counsel and incomprehensible in thought, whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of Adam — or of men —, to render to each according to his ways and according to the fruit of his devices. […]

32:18.t: You who show mercy to thousands and repay the iniquity of the fathers in the bosom of their sons after them. Great is the clemency of the Creator, to extend his mercy to a thousand generations and to show righteousness at once in the next generation, which itself, however, is mixed with mercy; for he does not punish the offender at once, but waits for repentance, so that, if the children have imitated the vices of their parents, the long-deferred punishment is repaid. Most mighty, great, powerful, the Lord of hosts — or of powers — is your name! These names indicate the power of the Creator; but properly the name of God is 'Father', which is revealed in the Gospel through the Lord, who says: Father, I have manifested your name to men.

32:19.t: Great in counsel: and does anyone dare to thrust himself into the secret of the Lord and to pass judgment on his judgments! And incomprehensible in thought: him whom thought does not comprehend, how can speech comprehend? Whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of Adam: in vain, then, does man think he can hide from the knowledge of God. And what he adds: to render to each according to his ways and according to the fruit of his devices, indicates this, that at times, because of his exceeding wisdom, his judgments seem unjust; a passage which the Apostle explains more fully to the Romans: do you not know that the goodness of God exhorts you to repentance? But according to your hardness and impenitent heart you treasure up for yourself wrath on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God. […]

32:20.t: You who set signs and portents in the land of Egypt even to this day, and in Israel and among men — or the earthborn — and made for yourself a name as this day. And you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and with portents and with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm and with great terror. And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers that you would give them, a land flowing with milk and honey. And they entered and possessed it; and they did not obey your voice and did not walk in your law. All that you commanded them to do they did not do; and all these evils befell them. From the general he passes to the particular and runs through in brief speech what he had bestowed specially on Israel. You who set, he says, signs and portents in the land of Egypt, by which Egypt was afflicted, even to this day, and in Israel and among men or the earthborn. […]

32:21.t: And you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt: he rightly said 'your people'; for at the time when it was brought out, it was serving the commands of the Lord. 'And you brought them out with signs and portents, by which Egypt was struck, and with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm and with great terror', when the Red Sea gave a way to the people of Israel as they crossed and overwhelmed the army of Egypt.

32:22.t: And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers that you would give them, namely, to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob. So they received the land of promise not by their own merit but by the virtues of their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey; for they could not yet take solid food, but were nourished with the honey and milk of infancy, or at any rate with honey and milk, the fruitfulness and abundance of all things.

32:23.t: And they entered and possessed it. And at once there was nothing between possession and disobedience; for plenty begets security, security negligence, negligence contempt. And they did not obey, he says, your voice, and did not walk in your law. In vain, then, did they promise in the wilderness, saying: all that the Lord commands we will do; for the reward lies not in the pledge but in the deed; so as to beat back the impudence of those who think that a man can fulfill all that he has promised he will do. All that you commanded them to do they did not do; and certainly they had promised that they would do it. And all these evils befell them; 'evils' to those who suffered them, but 'goods' according to the sentence of the Lord, which renders to each according to his ways.

32:24.t: Behold, siegeworks have been built against the city, that it may be taken, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans who fight against it, before the face of the sword and of famine and of pestilence; and whatever you have spoken has come to pass, as you yourself see; and you say to me, Lord God: Buy the field for silver and call witnesses, when the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans? It was the tenth year of King Zedekiah; for so it is written: the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah; then the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison. And rightly it is now said: 'behold, siegeworks have been built against the city, that it may be taken, and the city has been delivered into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they have no one to conquer, only people to capture; […]

32:27.t: Of course nothing is "too hard for the Lord." But if we choose to apply this principle so extravagantly and harshly in our capricious imaginations, we may then make out God to have done anything we please, on the ground that it was not impossible for him to do it. We must not suppose, however, because he is able to do all things, that he has done what he has not done. But we must inquire whether he has really done it. God could, if he had liked, have furnished humankind with wings to fly with, just as he gave wings to kites. We must not, however, run to the conclusion that he did this because he was able to do it. He might also have extinguished Praxeas and all other heretics at once; it does not follow, however, that he did, simply because he was able. For it was necessary that there should be both kites and heretics; it was necessary also that the Father should be crucified. […]

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying: Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh; shall for me difficult — or impossible — be — or be hidden from me — any word? Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will deliver this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it. And the Chaldeans shall come — and shall enter — fighting — or the Chaldeans shall come — against this city, and they shall set it on fire and burn it, and the houses on whose roofs they sacrificed to Baal and poured out libations to strange gods to provoke me. To sad things he joins glad ones, and after the overthrow of Jerusalem he promises a return to the captive people. And first he sets out the causes of the offense and of the righteous fury of God, so that the greater the guilt of the sinners, the more ample the clemency of the Creator toward the sinners. I, he says, am the Lord, the God of all flesh; […]

32:28.t: But what does it mean that the word came: therefore thus says the Lord? For what had gone before, that he should put a causal conjunction, saying: therefore thus says the Lord? 'Because', he says, 'it is my care to rule all things, to order everything and to render to each according to his ways, therefore I will deliver this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of the king of Babylon, and they shall take it'; for first it is surrounded by an army and is taken in Nebuchadnezzar's absence, and Zedekiah is led to Riblah and there is handed over to the king.

32:29.t: And the Chaldeans, he says, shall come, fighting against this city. Aquila did better, who for what is written, 'shall come', translated eiseleusontai, that is, 'shall enter' the city; for they were not absent, so as to 'come', since they had surrounded Jerusalem, as Scripture testifies: then the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and then: behold, siegeworks have been built against the city, that it may be taken, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans. How then shall they 'come' who were present? 'But those who were besieging the city shall enter', he says, 'and shall take it and set it on fire and burn it to the ground' — for the Hebrew word 'bau', by its ambiguity, means both 'shall come' and 'shall enter' — 'and the houses on whose roofs they sacrificed to Baal, the idol of the Sidonians, and poured out libations to strange gods to provoke me, so that they seemed to be heaping insults on the Creator, not through an error of religion but out of a kind of contentiousness'. […]

32:30.t: For the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah were continually — or alone — doing evil in my eyes from their youth. The Hebrew word 'ach' Aquila translated plēn, which signifies the conjunction 'nevertheless'; the first edition of Symmachus and the Seventy and Theodotion translated 'alone'; but the second edition of Symmachus rendered diolou, which we too have followed for the present, so as to say 'continually'. Let us then speak first according to the Hebrew: the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah continually doing evil. 'Both the ten', he says, 'and the two tribes did evil without ceasing, and their perseverance in the worst works was continual'. But if it was continual and always in the whole people, where is everlasting righteousness? But according to the Seventy, who said: alone doing evil, the question arises: had the other nations not done evil at the time when Israel and Judah were sinning? It is resolved thus: he who has the knowledge of God and departs from him sins alone in the eyes of God; […]

32:31.t: In my fury and in my indignation this city has become to me from the day on which they built it until this day, on which it is taken away from my sight. If from the time when the foundations of the city were laid until this day, when it was taken and set on fire and removed from the sight of the Lord, it was always in vice and provoked the indignation of the Lord against itself, where is — as we have often said already — the respite from sins?

32:32.t: Because of the wickedness, he says, of the sons of Israel and of the sons of Judah, which they did, provoking me to anger, they and their kings, their princes and their priests and their prophets, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. Because he had said above: in my fury and in my indignation this city has become to me from the day on which they built it until this day, on which it is taken away from my sight, and had shown that in general no one had been without sin, he now enumerates them part by part, both their kings and princes and priests and prophets, and, embracing everything in one word: the men, he says, of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And he rightly did not say: 'my kings and my princes and my priests and my prophets', but, because they had sinned: their kings and their princes and their priests and their prophets.

32:33.t: And they turned to me their backs and not their faces. According to what is written elsewhere: and they turned against me a withdrawing shoulder. For he who prays, with neck bowed, is cast prone upon the ground; but he who turns his back shows by the very gesture of his body that he disregards the one who threatens. 'And this', he says, 'they were doing'.

When I taught them at dawn and instructed them, and they would not listen, so as to receive discipline. 'When the darkness of error and all worship of idols had been put to flight, I desired daily to enlighten their hearts, confuted by my sentence, and to teach them what is right'. And to preserve free will, he joins on and says: and they would not listen, so as to receive discipline. There follows:

32:34.t: And they set their idols in the house in which my name is invoked, to pollute it. Not only at that time did Judah set up in the temple of God the statue of an idol of which we read at the beginning of Ezekiel, but to this day in the house of God, which is interpreted as the Church, or in the heart and soul of believers, an idol is set up when a new dogma is constructed and, according to Deuteronomy, is worshiped in secret; do you not know, he says, that you are the temple of God and the Spirit of God dwells in you?

32:35.t: And they built the high places — or altars — of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to initiate their sons and their daughters to Moloch. For 'initiate' in the Hebrew is written 'ebir', which Aquila and Symmachus translated 'lead across', the Seventy and Theodotion 'offer'. Of the 'valley of the sons of Hinnom', which in Hebrew is called 'Gehenna', we have spoken more fully above: that it lies below the springs of Siloam and, by its pleasantness, because it is a well-watered place, provoked the people to luxury, which the worship of idols follows. And it is to be noted that 'altars' and 'high places' are called 'bamoth' in the Hebrew language; this for the sake of those who are in doubt what this word means in the book of Samuel and of Kings. Moloch is the idol of the Ammonites, whose name is rendered as 'king'; and divine Scripture signifies that in that very place the people served not only the idol Baal but also Moab and all the demons.

Which I did not command them, nor did it come up into my heart, that they should do this abomination and lead Judah into sin. Properly, the tribes of Judah and Benjamin worshiped the images of the demons in the shrine of Baal and of Moloch; but it is evident that the ten tribes, which were called Samaria, Joseph and Ephraim, worshiped the golden calves in Bethel and Dan. And so great was the evil that was done by the people that God testifies that he never thought, nor did it come up into his heart, what they were going to do. But all these things are said anthrōpopathōs [in human terms].

32:36.t: And now, because of these things, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to this city, of which you say that it is delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword and by famine and by pestilence. Just as to those who hoped for help and trusted in the strength of the walls it is prophesied that Jerusalem is to be overthrown and the people on the very point of being captured, and before the captivity to perish by sword and famine and pestilence, so to those who despair and, after the overthrow of the city, expect no salvation, he promises his help, so that confidence and pride may merit a just sentence, and despair and humility the help of God.

32:37.t: Behold, I will gather them from all the lands to which I drove them out in my fury and in my wrath and in great indignation, and I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell confidently, and they shall be to me a people and I will be to them a God. And I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear me all their days, and that it may be well with them and with their sons after them. And I will strike with them an everlasting covenant — or I will appoint an eternal testament — and I will not cease to do them good, and I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not depart from me. And I will rejoice over them when I have done them good — or and I will visit them, to do them good —, and I will plant them in this land in truth — or in faith — with my whole heart and with my whole soul. […]

But you say, 'Was this therefore in accordance with the will of Him Who instituted by Moses that former commandment for those of old time? Yes, I answer; and I arrive at this conclusion, not of my own mind, but as having proof thereof in the prophetic Scriptures. For God has somewhere said by the voice of Isaiah, "And the laws of My people shall be made to disappear." How have the laws of the people been made to disappear? Because, as I said, they have been brought to nought by the manifestation of a new and better commandment, which the Son has spoken to us by Himself; and which also He proclaimed of old by the voice of Ezechiel, thus speaking of those of the race of Israel; "Behold, I will gather them from every land whither I have scattered them in My anger, and hot displeasure, and great wrath; […]
32:37.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

32:39.t: And one, he says, way — him who says: I am the way and the life and the truth —, that they may fear me all their days; for the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord. All, he says, their days: if this does not apply to the Jews, it must be taken of our people, with whom it has been and is and will be well, not only with themselves but also with their sons after them; for he has struck an everlasting covenant with us and will not cease henceforth to do us good. And what follows: and I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not depart from me, so grants free will that the very fear which is bestowed nevertheless remains the grace of the giver.

32:40.t: Because perseverance is much more difficult when the persecutor is engaged in preventing a man's perseverance; and therefore he is sustained in his perseverance unto death. Hence it is more difficult to have the former perseverance, easier to have the latter; but to Him to whom nothing is difficult it is easy to give both. For God has promised this, saying, "I will put my fear in their hearts, that they may not depart from me." And what else is this than, "Such and so great shall be my fear that I will put into their hearts that they will perseveringly cleave to me"?...When, therefore, God's hand is upon Him, that we depart not from God, assuredly God's work reaches to us (for this is God's hand); by which work of God we are caused to be abiding in Christ with God—not, as in Adam, departing from God. For "in Christ we have obtained a lot, being predestinated according to His purpose who worketh all things." This, therefore, is God's hand, not ours, that we depart not from God. […]

For that very pride has so stopped the ears of their heart that they do not hear, "For what hast thou that thou hast not received?" They do not hear, "Without me ye can do nothing;" they do not hear, "Love is of God;" they do not hear, "God hath dealt the measure of faith;" they do not hear, "The Spirit breatheth where it will," and, "They who are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God;" they do not hear, "No one can come unto me, unless it were given him of my Father;" they do not hear what Esdras writes, "Blessed is the Lord of our fathers, who hath put into the heart of the king to glorify His house which is in Jerusalem;" they do not hear what the Lord says by Jeremiah, "And I will put my fear into their heart, that they depart not from me; and I will visit them to make them good;" […]
32:40.s: Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 4:14

32:40.t: This grace He placed "in Him in whom we have obtained a lot, being predestinated according to the purpose of Him who worketh all things." And thus as He worketh that we come to Him, so He worketh that we do not depart. Wherefore it was said to Him by the mouth of the prophet, "Let Thy hand be upon the man of Thy right hand, and upon the Son of man whom Thou madest strong for Thyself, and we will not depart from Thee." This certainly is not the first Adam, in whom we departed from Him, but the second Adam, upon whom His hand is placed, so that we do not depart from Him. For Christ altogether with His members is—for the Church's sake, which is His body—the fulness of Him. When, therefore, God's hand is upon Him, that we depart not from God, assuredly God's work reaches to us (for this is God's hand); by which work of God we are caused to be abiding in Christ with God—not, as in Adam, departing from God. For "in Christ we have obtained a lot, being predestinated according to His purpose who worketh all things." […]

32:41.t: 'And when I have done them good', he says, 'I will rejoice and be glad', namely, that his creature has been saved; whence also there is joy among the angels in heaven over one sinner who repents. And I will plant them, he says, in this land in truth or — as the Seventy translated — in faith, so as to signify properly the Christian people, whose religion is faith. With my whole heart and with my whole soul: if these are the words of the Lord the Savior, the heart and soul are rightly believed to be his, who says in the Gospel: 'I have power to lay down my soul, and I have power to take it up again'; but if we take it as spoken in the person of God the Father, it must be understood according to that saying: your new moons and sabbaths and feast days my soul hates.

32:42.t: For thus says the Lord: As I have brought upon this people all this great evil, so I will bring upon them all the good that I speak to them. And fields shall be possessed in this land, of which you say that it is desolate because neither man nor beast has remained, and that it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans. Fields shall be bought with money and shall be written in a book, a seal shall be impressed, and a witness shall be called in the land of Benjamin and round about Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah and in the cities of the hill country and in the cities of the plain — or sephela — and in the cities of the nageb — that is: which are toward the south —, because I will turn their captivity, says the Lord. Although according to the letter these things went before in type after the return from the Chaldeans, when at the command of King Cyrus the people returned to Judea, yet spiritually they are fulfilled more truly and more fully in Christ and in the apostles. […]

32:44.t: Then fields were bought with money, that we might make for ourselves friends of the mammon of iniquity, who might receive us into the eternal tabernacles; and they were written in a book — doubtless the book of the living —, and the sign of the standard of the Lord's cross and victory was impressed, and witnesses were called, the martyrs and the whole choir of the saints. In the land of Benjamin, where the 'strength' of the Lord is; and round about Jerusalem, in which is the 'vision of peace' and eternal security; in the cities of Judah, in which is the true 'confession' of Christ; and in the cities of the hill country, one of which is that of which he says: a city set on a mountain cannot be hidden; and in the cities of the plain — which in Hebrew are called 'sephela' —, so that from the deep and low places we may advance across the level of the plains to the heights; and in the cities which are toward the south — for which the Seventy rendered 'nageb' —, where there is 'midday' and the full light of truth. […]

33:6.t: Yet we will add further what the same Jeremiah in another place mentions, in these words, concerning the wounds of the soul and the cures, in which nevertheless traces of the wounds have remained after the scar has closed over: "Behold, I will bring on its scar, and I will heal them together and manifest to them peace and faith; and I will turn the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Jerusalem." If, then, we have learned sufficiently from the prophet concerning the wounds and scars of souls and the cures and healings which are brought about with God as physician, behold now that soul concerning which God says that "I have brought on its scar." After wounds, without doubt, "he brings on a scar and health." "And I have healed them, and I will manifest to them peace and faith."

35:1.t: [Daniel 7:1] "In the first year of Belshazzar, King of Babylon, Daniel beheld a dream. And a vision of his head upon his bed. And when he wrote the dream down, he comprehended it in a few words and gave a brief summary of it, saying..." This section which we now undertake to explain, and also the subsequent section which we are going to discuss, is historically prior to the two previous sections. For this present section and that which follows it are recorded to have taken place in the first and third years of the reign of King Belshazzar (Jeremiah 39) [Jerome's citation of Jeremiah 39 seems quite pointless in this connection]. But the section which we read previously to the one just preceding this, is recorded to have taken place in the last year, indeed on the final day, of Belshaz-zar's reign. And we meet this phenomenon not only in Daniel but also in Jeremiah [cf. Jeremiah 35 and Jeremiah 34] and Ezekiel (Ezekiel 17), as we shall be able to show, if life spares us that long. […]
35:1.s: St. Jerome, Commentary on Daniel, CHAPTER SEVEN

35:6.t: The sons of Jonadab, we are told, drank neither wine nor strong drink and dwelled in tents pitched wherever night overtook them. According to the Psalter, they were the first to undergo captivity; for, when the Chaldaeans began to ravage Judah, they were compelled to take refuge in cities.Others may think what they like and follow each his own bent. But to me a town is a prison and solitude paradise. Why do we long for the bustle of cities, we whose very name speaks of loneliness? To fit him for the leadership of the Jewish people, Moses was trained for forty years in the wilderness. And it was not until after these that the shepherd of sheep became a shepherd of people. The apostles were fishers on Gennesaret before they became "fishers of people." But at the Lord's call they forsook all that they had, father, net and ship, and bore their cross daily without so much as a rod in their hands.

Jonadab (he is commended to us in the prophecy of Jeremiah) was a certain man, who had enjoined his sons not to drink wine, and not to dwell in houses, but in tents. But the commandment of the father the sons kept and observed, and by this earned a blessing from the Lord. Now the Lord had not commanded this, but their own father. But they so received it as though it were a commandment from the Lord their God; for even though the Lord had not commanded that they should drink no wine and should dwell in tents; yet the Lord had commanded that sons should obey their father. In this case alone a son ought not to obey his father, if his father should have commanded anything contrary to the Lord his God. For indeed the father ought not to be angry, when God is preferred before him. But when a father doth command that which is not contrary to God; he must be heard as God is: because to obey one’s father God hath enjoined. […]

What shall I say of the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab, of whom we are told that, when at the Lord's bidding the prophet Jeremiah offered them wine, they replied: "We drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying: Ye shall drink no wine, ye and your sons forever: and ye shall build no house, nor sow any seed, nor plant vineyards nor possess them: but ye shall dwell in tents all your days"? Wherefore also they were permitted to hear from the same prophet these words: "Thus saith the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel: there shall not fail a man from the stock of Jonadab the son of Rechab to stand in My sight all the days;" as all of them were not satisfied with merely offering tithes of their possessions, but actually refused property, and offered the rather to God themselves and their souls, for which no redemption can be made by man, as the Lord testifies in the gospel: "For what shall a man give in exchange for his own soul?"
35:6.s: The First Conference of Abbot Theonas, Chapter 4

35:15.t: Now, by these words of His, does the Lord clearly show all these points, that there is one King and Lord, the Father of all, of whom He had previously said, "Neither shalt thou swear by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King;" and that He had from the beginning prepared the marriage for His Son, and used, with the utmost kindness, to call, by the instrumentality of His servants, the men of the former dispensation to the wedding feast; and when they would not obey, He still invited them by sending out other servants, yet that even then they did not obey Him, but even stoned and slew those who brought them the message of invitation. He accordingly sent forth His armies and destroyed them, and burned down their city; but He called together from all the highways, that is, from all nations, guests to the marriage feast of His Son, as also He says by Jeremiah: "I have sent also unto you my servants the prophets to say, Return ye now, every man, from his very evil way, and amend your doings." […]

36:23.t: And what manner of prophet said this? Be not curious, nor overbusy. For many of the prophetic writings have been lost; and this one may see from the history of the Chronicles. For being negligent, and continually falling into ungodliness, some they suffered to perish, others they themselves burnt up and cut to pieces. The latter fact Jeremiah relates; the former, he who composed the fourth book of Kings, saying, that after a long time the book of Deuteronomy was hardly found, buried somewhere and lost. But if, when there was no barbarian there, they so betrayed their books, much more when the barbarians had overrun them.
36:23.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 9:6

37:15.t: Would anyone deny that Joseph was blessed in prison, where he interpreted dreams by the spirit of wisdom, revealing the truth and the sequence of future events? Would anyone deny that Isaiah was blessed when he was sawn in half? Jeremiah, when he was thrown into a pit? Daniel, when he stood unharmed among the lions, with the prophet's meal brought to him by an angel? Certainly, they were blessed not because they ate a meal that did not belong to them, but because they closed the mouths of the lions with their merits.
37:15.s: On Jacob and the Blessed Life 1.9.42

38:5.t: How am I distressed, think you, when I call to mind that on the festival days the multitudes assembled resemble the broad expanse of the sea, but now not even the smallest part of that multitude is gathered together here? Where are they now who oppress us with their presence on the feast days?… Now if they make the summer season their excuse: for I hear of their saying things of this kind, "the present stifling heat is excessive, the scorching sun is intolerable, we cannot bear being trampled and crushed in the crowd, and to be steaming all over with perspiration and oppressed by the heat and confined space:"… What then am I to say to those who advance these pretexts? […]
38:5.s: HOMILY TO THOSE WHO HAD NOT ATTENDED THE ASSEMBLY 2

40:1.t: Jeremiah, who was sanctified in the womb and was known in his mother's belly, enjoyed the high privilege because he was predestined to the blessing of virginity. And when all were captured and even the vessels of the temple were plundered by the king of Babylon, he alone was liberated by the enemy, did not know the insults of captivity and was supported by the conquerors; and Nebuchadnezzar, though he gave Nebuzaradan no charge concerning the Holy of Holies, did give him charge concerning Jeremiah. For that is the true temple of God and that is the Holy of Holies, which is consecrated to the Lord by pure virginity.

43:10.t: They could have stayed there, then, and were not afraid, but surely the heavenly hand that had dragged them thither to punish the vices of the Spanish compelled them also to cross the straits to devastate Africa. In fact, they themselves confessed that they did not act of their own volition, for they were driven and urged on by a divine command. From this we may learn how great are our misdoings, since to destroy and punish us the barbarians are compelled to move against their will, following the words of the devastator of the land of Israel, the king of the Assyrians, when he said: '' And now without the will of the Lord am I come up against this land? The Lord said unto me, 'Go up against this land, to destroy it.' " And elsewhere the Sacred Word says: "Therefore thus saith the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel: 'Behold, I will send and take Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon, my servant, and when he cometh, he shall smite the land of Egypt.' […]
43:10.s: On the Government of God, Book 7, Chapter 13

44:8.t: Then, since they kept on in a state of incurable madness, and were not to be sobered even by the rest being carried away, he first exhorts them to remain there. But when they kept not up to this, but deserted to Egypt, this indeed He allowed them, but requires of them not to desert to irreligion as well as to Egypt. But when they did not comply in this either, He sendeth the prophet along with them, so that they might not after all suffer total wreck. For since they did not follow Him when He called, He next followeth them to discipline them, and hinder their being hurried further into vice, and as a father full of affection does a child who takes all treatment in the same peevish way, conducting him about everywhere with himself, and following him about. This was the reason why He sent not Jeremiah only into Egypt, but also Ezekiel into Babylon, and they did not refuse to go. For when they found their Master love the people exceedingly, they continued themselves to do so likewise.

44:21.t: We cannot therefore console ourselves at all on these grounds, that is, by saying that the former extravagances are not now being committed in all our cities. For the only reason for their abandonment is that cities where they were carried on in the past are no longer in existence, or that in the places where such things used to be done, [means are lacking] to perform them. Thus the spectacles are no longer possible in the cities where they were formerly performed; as God himself said to sinners through his prophet: "The Lord remembered these things and it came into his mind, and the Lord could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings and because of the abominations which ye have committed; therefore is your land a desolation, and an astonishment and a curse." So it has come to pass that the greater part of the Roman world is become a desolation and an astonishment and a curse.
44:21.s: On the Government of God, Book 6, Chapter 8

46:25.t: Moreover the prophet Jeremiah too understands Amon, or No, as Alexandria in the vision against Egypt, to which he says: Egypt is a beautiful heifer; a goader will come to her from the north. He also adds this more plainly: The daughter of Egypt is confounded, she has been delivered into the hand of the people of the north, says the Lord of powers, the God of Israel. Behold, I will visit upon Amon Menno, that is, upon the people from Alexandria. For Amon, as we have said, means peoples, men the preposition 'from', and No Alexandria. And I will visit, he says, upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt and upon her gods; and upon her kings, and upon Pharaoh, and upon those who hope in him; and I will give them into the hands of those who seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants.

48:10.t: Since the Lord said: “Sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me”; and again: “Sell that ye have, and give alms”; I consider that the man who leaves his family with such an end in view ought not to feel contemptuously towards his possessions, but to make an accurate survey of them all, as consecrated henceforward to the Lord, and dispose of them with all care, either personally if he has the power and necessary experience, or through men who have been chosen for the work after careful testing and have given proof of their powers of faithful and wise administration. He must realise that it is dangerous either to leave them to his relations or to dispose of them through any chance-comer. For if the man who is entrusted with the care of the King’s property, though often he has filched nothing from the store but only lost by neglect the interest he might have gained, is not absolved from blame; […]

Since the apostle says: “Let all things be done decently and in order,” we reckon that to be a decent and orderly manner of life among the society of the faithful, in which the principle of the members of the body is preserved. So that one has the powers of the eye, being entrusted with the general oversight, both approving what has been done, and foreseeing and arranging what is to be done; and another the powers of the ear or hand in respect of hearing or doing what is necessary—and so on. Know therefore that just as with our members it is dangerous for any one limb to neglect its functions, or not to make use of another for the purpose for which it was made by God the Creator—for if the hand or foot obey not the guidance of the eye, the one will inevitably touch dangerous things to the destruction of the whole body, and the other will knock against them or be precipitated from a height; […]

Wherefore on account of what has been said, and for many other similar reasons, it is essential that those who distribute necessaries to the brotherhood should be free absolutely from favouritism and contention. Indeed they ought to be conscious of such a disposition in themselves and to show such zeal—both they and those that perform the other works for the service of the brethren—as if they were serving not men but the Lord Himself, Who of His great goodness reckons as done unto Himself the honour and zeal shown to those who are dedicated to Him, and promises in return an inheritance in the kingdom of heaven. For He says: “Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For inasmuch as ye did it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye did it unto me.” And on the other hand we must recognise the peril of negligence, remembering the words: “Cursed is he that doeth the work of the Lord negligently.” […]

When you repeat a psalm, consider whose words you are repeating and delight yourself more with true contrition of soul, than with the pleasantness of a trilling voice. For God sets a higher value on the tears of one thus praising him, than on the beauty of his voice; as the prophet says, "Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling." Now, where there are fear and trembling, there is no lifting up of the voice, but humility of mind with lamentation and tears. Display diligence in all thy doings; for it is written, "Cursed is the man who carelessly performs the work of the Lord." Let grace grow in you with years; let righteousness increase with age; and let your faith appear the more perfect the older you become; for Jesus, who has left us an example how to live, increased not only in years as respected his body, but in wisdom and spiritual grace before God and men. Reckon all the time in which you do not perceive yourself growing better as positively lost.

Whoever then is aiming at this condition, which we have mentioned, will seek the grace of satisfaction by daily fasting and mortification of heart and body, for, as it is written, "Without shedding of blood there is no remission;" and this not without good reason. For "flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God." And therefore one who would withhold "the sword of the spirit which is the word of God" from this shedding of blood certainly comes under the lash of that curse of Jeremiah's; for "Cursed," says he "is he who withholds his sword from blood." For this is the sword which for our good sheds that bad blood whereby the material of our sins lives; and cuts Off and pares away everything carnal and earthly which it finds to have grown up in the members of our soul; and makes men die to sin and live to God, and flourish with spiritual virtues. […]

Those also who take the main part of their offerings, i.e., their offices and actions, to benefit the flesh for their own use, but leave the remains of them and a tiny portion for the Lord, these the Divine Word thus condemns as fraudulent workmen: "Cursed is he that doeth the work of the Lord fraudulently."
48:10.s: The First Conference of Abbot Theonas, Chapter 22

48:10.t: FoR as unbounded glory hereafter is promised to those who faithfully serve God and cleave to Him according to the rule of this system; so the severest penalties are in store for those who have carried it out carelessly and coldly, and have failed to show to Him fruits of holiness corresponding to what they professed or what they were believed by men to be. For "it is better," as Scripture says, "that a man should not vow rather than that he should vow and not pay;" and "Cursed is he that doeth the work of the Lord carelessly." Therefore you were for a long while declined by us, not as if we did not des re with all our hearts to secure your salvation and the salvation of all, nor as if we did not careto go to meet even afar off those who are longing to be converted to Christ; […]
48:10.s: The Twelve Books on the Institutes of the Coenobia, Book 4, Chapter 33

48:10.t: If persons by no means ignorant of the medicinal art were to see a sore that required lancing and yet refused to lance it, certainly by their mere inactivity they would be guilty of a brother's death. Let them see, then, in how great guilt they are involved who, knowing the sores of souls, neglect to cure them by the lancing of words. And so, it is well said through the prophet, "Cursed is one who keeps back his sword from blood." For to keep back the sword from blood is to hold back the word of preaching from the killing of the carnal life. Of which sword it is said again, "And my sword shall devour flesh."

As to those whom he sees to be of a weak will and of feeble thought he combates them vehemently from the beginning by submitting them to heavy and terrible temptations, in order to make them taste the nature of his evil from the very beginning of the way. In this way he intends to instill into them a horror of the first battle so that this way shall appear to them difficult to walk. And if the beginning is very difficult, who could endure to the end, facing all the battles which are ranged in the middle? Thus they will not again venture to withstand him or to look for other help, on account of their being totally occupied with the thought of his attacks. And when he has pressed them a little vehemently they take to flight. Or better: God lets him oppress them, without helping them in any way because they have engaged in the battle of the Lord, with a cold heart and hesitatingly. Cursed is every one who performs the work of the Lord without diligence, retaining his hand from bloodshed. […]

48:19.t: Aroer: dug under. But better: tamarisk.

48:29.t: Let heretics give heed.… "His haughtiness and his arrogance and his pride and the loftiness of his heart I know," says the Lord, "because his strength is not according to the loftiness of his boasts."

49:9.t: Jeremiah likewise, though with the order changed: If grape-gatherers had come upon you, would they not have left a cluster? If thieves in the night, they would surely have seized what was enough for them. But I have uncovered Esau, I have revealed his hidden things, and he shall not be able to hide. What he says is this: If thieves and robbers, who are accustomed by night to dig through houses and to seize what is in the houses, had come in to you, and, hidden by the darkness, had gone round the corners of your house, they would surely have carried off what they thought could be enough for them, and would have left something in your dwelling, either through being sated or through not knowing of it. If grape-gatherers had come into your vineyard, and wished either to lay it waste as enemies or, hired by you, to harvest it, however diligent their vintage had been, they would still have left among the branches clusters hidden by the vines and leaves. […]

49:15.t: Jeremiah, of whom we made mention above, agrees in almost the same words, saying: Behold, I have given you small among the nations: contemptible among men; your arrogance has deceived you, and the pride of your heart, you who dwell in the caverns of the rock and strive to lay hold of the height of the hill; when you have exalted your nest like the eagle, from there I will drag you down, says the Lord. In prophetic interpretation we ought to follow our custom, so as first to lay the foundations of history, then, if we can, to raise up lofty towers and the tops of roofs. O Edom, he says, though you are the least among all the nations round about, and small in number in comparison with the other peoples, you are lifted up by pride beyond your strength. And though you dwell in grottoes, nay rather in the caverns of the rocks, lowly and poor, and not possessing the lofty roofs of buildings, you are borne up on high like an eagle, and you swell so much in thought that you believe you dwell among the stars; […]
